Net Cash Received from Disposal of Fixed Assets and Other Long-term Assets in Next Period
下期资产处置现金净流入
处置固定资产收回的现金净额
处置长期资产收回的现金净额
nodes.definition: Net cash proceeds from disposal of fixed assets in the next period refers to the net amount of cash that an enterprise expects to recover in the next accounting period (such as the next reporting period or budget period) through the sale, retirement, or impairment of fixed assets, intangible assets, and other long-term assets, after deducting the estimated related cash expenditures incurred during the disposal process. It reflects the expected impact of the enterprise's planned disposal of long-term assets on future cash flows.

nodes.name: Net Cash Received from Disposal of Fixed Assets, Intangible Assets and Other Long-term Assets
aliases: 处置长期资产收回的现金净额
nodes.definition: Net cash received from disposal of fixed assets, intangible assets and other long-term assets refers to the net amount of cash actually received by an enterprise from disposing of fixed assets, intangible assets and other long-term assets through sale, retirement, etc., during the reporting period, after deducting cash payments directly related to the disposal activities (such as disposal costs, related taxes and fees). This indicator is an important component of cash flows from investing activities in the cash flow statement, reflecting the cash recovery situation from the disposal of long-term assets.

nodes.name: Net Cash Received from Disposal of Fixed Assets, Intangible Assets and Other Long-term Assets in Year k
aliases: Cash Inflow from Disposal of Long-term Assets
Net Cash Received from Disposal of Fixed Assets, Intangible Assets and Other Long-term Assets
处置固定资产等收回的现金净额
处置长期资产收回的现金净额
长期资产处置现金净流入
nodes.definition: Refers to the net amount of cash actually received by an enterprise in the k-th fiscal year from the sale, retirement, or transfer of fixed assets, intangible assets, and other long-term assets (such as long-term prepaid expenses), minus the cash directly paid during the disposal process (such as disposal costs, related taxes and fees, etc.). It reflects the cash inflow generated by the enterprise from the disposal of long-term assets and is an important component of cash flows from investing activities in the cash flow statement.

nodes.name: Net Cash Received from Disposal of Fixed Assets, Intangible Assets, and Other Long-term Assets in Year k
Net Cash Received from Disposal of Fixed Assets, etc. for the Next Period
Net Cash Received from Disposal of Subsidiaries and Other Business Units
aliases: Net Cash Inflow from Disposal of Subsidiaries
处置子公司收到的现金净额
处置营业单位现金净流入
nodes.definition: Net cash received from disposal of subsidiaries and other business units is an item reported in the investing activities section of the statement of cash flows. It reflects the net cash inflow ultimately obtained from a specific transaction involving the sale or transfer of a subsidiary or other business unit (such as a branch or business line), calculated as the total cash actually received minus related expenses paid to complete the disposal (e.g., intermediary fees, taxes) and minus the cash and cash equivalents held by the disposed unit itself. If the calculation results in a negative amount (i.e., a net outflow), it is reported in other investing activities cash outflows on the statement of cash flows.

nodes.name: Net Cash Received from Disposal of Subsidiaries and Other Business Units for the Next Period
Net Cash Received from Disposal of Subsidiaries and Other Business Units in Year k
aliases: Cash Inflow from Disposal of Subsidiaries
Net Cash Received from Disposal of Subsidiaries and Other Business Units
处置子公司收到的现金净额
处置营业单位现金净流入
nodes.definition: Refers to the net cash inflow amount ultimately calculated in year k from the actual cash received by the enterprise through the sale or disposal of its subsidiaries or other business units (such as business segments), minus the direct costs associated with the disposal (such as handling fees, taxes, etc.), and further minus the cash and cash equivalents held by the disposed units themselves. This amount reflects the net cash return obtained by the enterprise due to business contraction or restructuring.

nodes.name: Net Cash Received from Disposal of Subsidiaries and Other Business Units in the Subsequent Period
aliases: Cash Inflow from Disposal of Business Units
Net Cash Received from Disposal of Subsidiaries and Other Business Units
处置子公司收到的现金净额
处置营业单位现金净流入
nodes.definition: Net cash received from disposal of subsidiaries and other business units in the subsequent period refers to the net cash inflow ultimately generated when an enterprise disposes of its subsidiaries or other business units in a future period (e.g., the next accounting period), calculated as the total cash actually received minus related disposal expenses and further minus the cash and cash equivalents held by the disposed units themselves. This amount reflects the anticipated net cash impact of such asset disposal activities in the future period.

nodes.name: Net Change
nodes.definition: Net change is the difference between the current period's closing price and the previous period's closing price for a security, indicating the absolute price movement over the specified interval. It can be positive (price increase) or negative (price decrease).

formulas.source_formula: Net Change = Current Closing Price - Previous Closing Price
Percentage Change = (Current Close - Previous Close) ÷ Previous Close × 100
Price Change = ((New Price − Original Price) ÷ Original Price) × 100

nodes.name: Net Charge-Off
nodes.definition: Net charge-off (NCO) represents the portion of delinquent or defaulted loans written off as uncollectible after accounting for recoveries. It is calculated as gross charge-offs minus recoveries and is used to assess credit cost, asset quality, and provisioning needs in financial institutions.

formulas.source_formula: Net Charge-Off = Gross Charge-Offs - Recoveries

nodes.name: Net Charge-Off Ratio
nodes.definition: The net charge-off ratio measures the proportion of a lender’s average total loans that are written off as uncollectible during a period. It is calculated as net charge-offs (gross charge-offs minus recoveries) divided by average total loans. Lower values indicate better asset quality and lower credit risk.

formulas.source_formula: Net Charge-Off Ratio = Net Charge-Offs ÷ Average Total Loans

nodes.name: Net Consumption
nodes.definition: Net consumption refers to the quantity of materials directly constituting the engineering entity or product itself that is necessarily consumed in production activities such as construction and installation projects, excluding any losses during processing or construction. It serves as the fundamental raw data for calculating material consumption quotas, loss rates, and total consumption.

nodes.name: Net Consumption Quantity
nodes.definition: Net consumption quantity refers to the amount of material directly required to constitute the product or project entity during production or construction, excluding any losses incurred during processing or operations. It serves as a fundamental indicator for calculating material consumption quotas and conducting cost accounting.

formulas.source_formula: Net Consumption Quantity = Consumption Quantity × (1 - Loss Rate)
Net Cost Change (Long Hedge) = Physical Price Change - Futures Profit/Loss

nodes.name: Net Cost of Main Business
nodes.definition: Net Cost of Main Business refers to the net cost incurred by an enterprise to obtain current main business revenue, after deducting relevant adjustments. It is an intermediate indicator used in financial analysis, often employed to calculate efficiency ratios such as accounts payable turnover ratio, in order to more accurately reflect the cost expenditure level of core business operations.

formulas.source_formula: Net Cost of Main Business = Cost of Main Business - Write-off of Inventory Impairment Loss - Cost-related Returns and Allowances
Net Cost of Spread = (Cost of Higher Strike - Revenue from Lower Strike) × Shares per Contract
Net Cost or Credit = (Put Premium - Call Premium) × Shares per Contract
Net Credit = Sell Premium - Buy Premium
Net Credit = Premium Received (High) - Premium Paid (Low)

nodes.name: Net Credit Sales
nodes.definition: Net credit sales refer to the net amount of sales revenue actually receivable from customers during a specific period, after deducting items such as sales returns, sales allowances, and sales discounts from total sales. It serves as a key foundational data point for calculating financial metrics such as accounts receivable turnover ratio.

nodes.name: Net Current Asset Value per Share
aliases: Net Current Asset Value Per Share
Net Current Asset Value Per Share (NCAVPS)
nodes.definition: Net Current Asset Value Per Share (NCAVPS) measures the excess of current assets over total liabilities and preferred stock on a per-share basis. Rooted in Benjamin Graham’s net-net approach, it indicates the liquidation-style floor value attributable to common shareholders for each share, often used by value investors to identify deeply undervalued stocks.
primary_aliases: Net Current Asset Value Per Share (NCAVPS)

formulas.source_formula: Net Current Asset Value Per Share (NCAVPS) = (Current Assets - (Total Liabilities + Preferred Stock)) ÷ Shares Outstanding
supporting_source_formulas: Net Current Asset Value Per Share (NCAVPS) = (Current Assets - (Total Liabilities + Preferred Stock)) ÷ Shares Outstanding
Net Current Asset Value per Share = (Current Assets - (Total Liabilities + Preferred Stock)) ÷ Shares Outstanding

nodes.name: Net Debt
nodes.definition: Net debt is a composite financial metric that measures a company's actual debt repayment pressure, reflecting the net amount of debt that the company actually needs to repay after deducting quickly realizable financial assets. Its core purpose is to measure the debt capital truly invested in production and operations, serving as a key parameter for evaluating the degree of financial leverage utilization, debt repayment risk, and the safety of the capital chain.

formulas.source_formula: Net Debt = Financial Liabilities - Financial Assets
supporting_source_formulas: Net Debt = Financial Liabilities - Financial Assets

formulas.source_formula: Net Debt = Total Liabilities - Cash and Cash Equivalents
supporting_source_formulas: Net Debt = Total Liabilities - Cash and Cash Equivalents

formulas.source_formula: Net Debt = Short-term Borrowings + Long-term Borrowings + Bonds Payable + Current Portion of Non-current Liabilities - Ending Cash and Cash Equivalents

nodes.name: Net Debt Financing Flow
nodes.definition: Net debt financing flow refers to the after-tax cash flow that can be distributed to creditors, reflecting the net cash changes generated by debt financing activities. It is typically used in managerial cash flow statement analysis to calculate entity free cash flow.

formulas.source_formula: Net Debt Financing Flow = After-tax Interest Expense + Repayment of Debt Principal + Increase in Excess Financial Assets

nodes.name: Net Debt Increase
nodes.definition: Net debt increase refers to the net change in a company's total debt over a specific period, typically calculated using the formula 'Net Debt Increase = Total Debt at Period End - Total Debt at Period Beginning'. It is a composite metric rather than a fundamental data point and is commonly used in financial analyses such as equity cash flow analysis.

nodes.name: Net Debt Market Value
nodes.definition: Net debt market value refers to the net value of a company's total debt at market value minus its holdings of cash and cash equivalents, reflecting the actual interest-bearing debt burden borne by the company. It is commonly used in enterprise valuation and is a key component in calculating entity value or equity value.

nodes.name: Net Debt Per Capita
nodes.definition: Net debt per capita measures the amount of a government’s net debt attributable to each resident. It is calculated as total debt (short-term plus long-term) minus cash and cash equivalents, divided by the population, and is used to assess the burden of indebtedness per person and compare fiscal positions across jurisdictions.

formulas.source_formula: Net Debt per Capita = (Short-Term Debt + Long-Term Debt - Cash and Cash Equivalents) ÷ Population

nodes.name: Net Debt Value
nodes.definition: Net debt value refers to the net amount of debt remaining after deducting cash and cash equivalents from a company's total debt when evaluating corporate value. It reflects the actual interest-bearing debt burden that the company needs to bear and is a core concept commonly used in measuring corporate financial risk and conducting business valuation.

nodes.name: Net Debt at Period End
nodes.definition: Net Debt at Period End is a composite financial metric used to measure an enterprise's true net debt burden at a specific point in time (typically the balance sheet date). It reflects the total amount of debt the enterprise actually needs to repay after deducting its own holdings of highly liquid financial assets. This metric is commonly used in enterprise valuation, solvency analysis, and capital structure management, and is referenced in calculating related metrics such as 'Net Investment for the Period'.

formulas.source_formula: Net Debt at Period End = Total Liabilities - Cash and Cash Equivalents
Net Debt at Period End = Total Assets - Total Equity - Cash and Cash Equivalents

nodes.name: Net Debt-to-EBITDA Ratio
aliases: 净债务与息税折旧摊销前利润比率
nodes.definition: The Net Debt-to-EBITDA Ratio measures a company's leverage by comparing net debt (total debt minus cash and cash equivalents) to EBITDA. It indicates how many years of EBITDA would be required to repay net debt, assuming both remain constant. Lower values suggest stronger debt coverage and lower financial risk, while negative values indicate excess cash relative to debt.

operands.metric: Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation and Amortization (EBITDA)

formulas.source_formula: Net Debt-to-EBITDA Ratio = (Short-term Debt + Long-term Debt - Cash and Cash Equivalents) ÷ EBITDA

nodes.name: Net Decrease in Non-Interest-Bearing Liabilities
nodes.definition: Net decrease in non-interest-bearing liabilities is a change metric that reflects the reduction amount in the total liabilities not requiring interest payments between two points in time (typically the beginning and end of a period). It is commonly used as one of the adjustment items in calculating net cash flow from operating activities under the indirect method.

operands.metric: Total Non-Interest-Bearing Liabilities at Beginning of Period
Total Non-Interest-Bearing Liabilities at End of Period

formulas.source_formula: Net Decrease in Non-Interest-Bearing Liabilities = Total Non-Interest-Bearing Liabilities at Beginning of Period - Total Non-Interest-Bearing Liabilities at End of Period

nodes.name: Net Decrease in Non-interest-bearing Liabilities in the Next Period
aliases: Net Decrease in Non-Interest-Bearing Liabilities for the Next Period
下期无息负债净变动（减少）
nodes.definition: Net decrease in non-interest-bearing liabilities in the next period refers to the net reduction in the total amount of a company's liabilities that do not require interest payments (such as accounts payable, employee compensation payable, advance receipts, etc.) during the next accounting period. This metric is calculated by comparing the total non-interest-bearing liabilities at the beginning and end of the next period and serves as a key adjustment item for calculating the net cash flow from operating activities in the next period under the indirect method.

operands.metric: Total Non-interest-bearing Liabilities at the Beginning of the Next Period
Total Non-interest-bearing Liabilities at the End of the Next Period

formulas.source_formula: Net Decrease in Non-interest-bearing Liabilities in the Next Period = Total Non-interest-bearing Liabilities at the Beginning of the Next Period - Total Non-interest-bearing Liabilities at the End of the Next Period

operands.metric: Total Liabilities at the Beginning of the Next Period
Total Interest-bearing Liabilities at the Beginning of the Next Period
Total Liabilities at the End of the Next Period
Total Interest-bearing Liabilities at the End of the Next Period

formulas.source_formula: Net Decrease in Non-interest-bearing Liabilities in the Next Period = Total Liabilities at the Beginning of the Next Period - Total Interest-bearing Liabilities at the Beginning of the Next Period - (Total Liabilities at the End of the Next Period - Total Interest-bearing Liabilities at the End of the Next Period)

nodes.name: Net Dividend
aliases: Dividend Net of Tax and Fees
nodes.definition: Net dividend is the amount of dividend an investor actually receives after deducting applicable taxes and fees from the gross dividend, reflecting the cash inflow attributable to equity holdings post obligations.

formulas.source_formula: Net Dividend = Gross Dividend - (Gross Dividend × Tax Rate) - (Gross Dividend × Fees and Expenses Rate)

nodes.name: Net Dividends Paid to Shareholders
nodes.definition: Net dividends paid to shareholders refer to the total cash dividends actually distributed by a company to its shareholders over a specific period (such as a fiscal year), typically including cash dividends paid to both common and preferred shareholders. This represents a significant component of the company's cash outflows and reflects the company's profit distribution to its shareholders.

nodes.name: Net Domestic Product
nodes.definition: Net Domestic Product (NDP) is a national accounts measure equal to Gross Domestic Product (GDP) minus depreciation (capital consumption allowance). It reflects the value of goods and services produced within a country after accounting for the consumption of fixed capital, providing a gauge of sustainable economic output.

formulas.source_formula: Net Domestic Product = Gross Domestic Product - Depreciation
Net Effect = Initial Change + Hedge Change

nodes.name: Net Equity Financing Flow
nodes.definition: Net equity financing flow refers to the net cash inflow or outflow generated by a company through equity financing activities such as issuing or repurchasing shares within a specific period.

formulas.source_formula: Net Equity Financing Flow = Dividend Distribution - Equity Capital Issuance

nodes.name: Net Equity Investment
nodes.definition: Net equity investment refers to the net capital expenditure funded by shareholders' equity to maintain and expand operations, typically used in calculating free cash flow to equity, and serves as a key metric for measuring the scale of capital contributions by shareholders.

formulas.source_formula: Net Equity Investment = Capital Expenditure + Increase in Working Capital - Depreciation and Amortization

nodes.name: Net Equity Investment Per Share for the Year
Net Equity Investment for the Year
nodes.definition: Net equity investment for the year refers to the net investment at the shareholder equity level, reflecting the portion of funds contributed by shareholders for enterprise development.

nodes.name: Net Estate Value
nodes.definition: Net estate value is the residual value of a decedent's estate after deducting liabilities (debts, taxes, and administration expenses) from the adjusted gross estate. For estate tax and distribution purposes, major gifts made within three years before death may be included in the gross estate, forming the adjusted gross estate before liabilities are deducted.

formulas.source_formula: Net Estate Value = Adjusted Gross Estate - Liabilities

nodes.name: Net Expense Ratio
nodes.definition: Net expense ratio represents the ongoing fund operating expenses borne by investors after accounting for fee waivers, reimbursements, or rebates. It reflects the actual cost of owning a mutual fund or ETF and is calculated by subtracting fee waivers from the gross expense ratio.

formulas.source_formula: Net Expense Ratio = Gross Expense Ratio - Fee Waivers

nodes.name: Net Export
nodes.definition: Net export represents the difference between a nation's total value of exports and total value of imports over a specific period. A positive value indicates a trade surplus, while a negative value indicates a trade deficit. Net exports are a key component of the balance of trade and the expenditure approach to GDP, offering insights into external demand and international competitiveness.

formulas.source_formula: Net Exports = Total Exports - Total Imports

nodes.name: Net Exports
nodes.definition: Net exports refer to the difference between the total value of a country or region's exports and imports of goods and services over a specific period (typically a year, half-year, quarter, or month). It reflects the balance of its foreign trade and is a key component in calculating nominal GDP. When exports exceed imports, it is called a trade surplus; when net exports are negative, it is called a trade deficit.

operands.metric: Total Imports of Goods and Services

formulas.source_formula: Net Exports = Exports - Imports

nodes.name: Net Exports of Goods and Services
nodes.definition: Net exports of goods and services refer to the difference between the total value of a country's exports and imports of goods and services over a specific period. It is a core indicator for measuring trade activity under the current account in the balance of payments and a key component in the expenditure approach to calculating Gross Domestic Product (GDP).

operands.metric: Total Exports of Goods and Services
Total Imports of Goods and Services

formulas.source_formula: Net Exports of Goods and Services = Total Exports of Goods and Services - Total Imports of Goods and Services

nodes.name: Net Exports of Goods and Services at Constant Prices
aliases: Constant Price Net Exports of Goods and Services
实际货物和服务净出口
nodes.definition: Net exports of goods and services at constant prices is a price-adjusted measure of net exports, used to eliminate the effects of price changes and reflect the net external demand in real output. It is a key component in calculating real GDP. It is derived by deflating nominal net exports with a price index to measure the contribution of net exports to real economic activity.

operands.metric: Nominal Net Exports of Goods and Services

formulas.source_formula: Net Exports of Goods and Services at Constant Prices = Nominal Net Exports of Goods and Services ÷ Goods and Services Price Deflator

operands.metric: Exports of Goods and Services at Constant Prices
Imports of Goods and Services at Constant Prices

formulas.source_formula: Net Exports of Goods and Services at Constant Prices = Exports of Goods and Services at Constant Prices - Imports of Goods and Services at Constant Prices

nodes.name: Net Exposure
nodes.definition: Net exposure measures a portfolio’s directional market exposure by subtracting the market value of short positions from the market value of long positions. It indicates whether the portfolio is net long or net short and the magnitude of its directional risk, commonly used in long-short and market-neutral strategies.

formulas.source_formula: Net Exposure = Long Positions - Short Positions
supporting_source_formulas: Net Exposure = Long Positions - Short Positions

nodes.name: Net Fair Value Adjustment of Assets
aliases: 可辨认净资产公允价值调整
nodes.definition: Net fair value adjustment of assets refers to the calculated adjustment amount derived from comparing the fair value of identifiable net assets with their book value under the equity method of accounting or in business combinations, accounting for differences such as asset appreciation, depreciation adjustments, etc. It is a composite metric that requires calculation based on other underlying data.

formulas.source_formula: Net Fair Value Adjustment of Assets = Total Adjusted Assets - Total Book Value of Assets

nodes.name: Net Fair Value of Identifiable Net Assets
Net Financial Debt
nodes.definition: Net financial debt is the difference between a company's financial liabilities and financial assets, indicating its reliance on external financing.

formulas.source_formula: Net Financial Debt = Financial Liabilities - Financial Assets

nodes.name: Net Financial Leverage
nodes.definition: Net financial leverage is the ratio of net debt to shareholders' equity, used to measure the degree of financial risk arising from a company's use of net debt financing. In the modified DuPont analysis system, it serves as a key metric for calculating return on equity and leverage contribution.

formulas.source_formula: Net Financial Leverage = Net Debt ÷ Shareholders' Equity

nodes.name: Net Financing Amount
aliases: Net Cash Flow from Financing Activities
筹资活动产生的现金流量净额
nodes.definition: Net financing amount, also known as net cash flow from financing activities, refers to the difference between cash inflows from financing activities such as absorbing investments and borrowing, and cash outflows from financing activities such as debt repayment and dividend distribution. It reflects the net cash amount obtained or consumed by the enterprise through financing activities.

operands.metric: Other Cash Received Related to Financing Activities
Cash Paid for Dividends, Profits or Interest Payments
Other Cash Paid Related to Financing Activities

formulas.source_formula: Net Financing Amount = Cash Received from Capital Contributions + Cash Received from Borrowings + Other Cash Received Related to Financing Activities - Cash Paid for Debt Repayment - Cash Paid for Dividends, Profits or Interest Payments - Other Cash Paid Related to Financing Activities

nodes.name: Net Fixed Assets
aliases: Net Book Value of Fixed Assets
nodes.definition: Net fixed assets refer to the remaining book value of a company's fixed assets after deducting accumulated depreciation and impairment provisions, reflecting the current actual value and the degree of wear and tear of the fixed assets.

nodes.name: Net Foreign Assets (NFA)
nodes.definition: Net Foreign Assets represent the stock of a nation's foreign assets minus its foreign liabilities at a point in time, indicating whether the nation is a net international creditor (positive NFA) or debtor (negative NFA).

formulas.source_formula: Net Foreign Assets = Foreign Assets - Foreign Liabilities

nodes.name: Net Foreign Factor Income
aliases: 来自国外的净要素收入
nodes.definition: Net Foreign Factor Income (NFFI) is the net income that residents of a country earn from abroad minus the income that foreign residents earn domestically. It equals the difference between Gross National Product (GNP) and Gross Domestic Product (GDP), capturing the impact of cross-border labor and capital income flows on national income.

formulas.source_formula: Net Foreign Factor Income = Gross National Product - Gross Domestic Product

nodes.name: Net Fund Flow
nodes.definition: Net fund flow is the difference between total cash inflows into and total cash outflows from a financial asset or fund during a specific period, indicating the net movement of investor capital.

formulas.source_formula: Net Fund Flow = Inflows - Outflows

nodes.name: Net GST Payable
aliases: GST Net of Input Tax Credit
nodes.definition: Net GST payable represents the effective goods and services tax due after deducting input tax credits previously paid. It is calculated by applying the GST rate to the taxable value (base price plus added value) and subtracting the prior-stage GST already paid.

formulas.source_formula: Net GST Payable = (Base Price + Added Value) × GST Rate - Previous Tax
Net Gain/Loss = Realized Capital Gains - Realized Capital Losses

nodes.name: Net Gains from Changes in Fair Value
nodes.definition: Net gains from changes in fair value refer to the net profit or loss arising from changes in the fair value of assets (such as trading financial assets, investment properties, etc.) or liabilities measured at fair value with changes recognized in profit or loss, comparing the fair value at the reporting date to the fair value at the previous reporting date or initial recognition date. It is an important item in the income statement reflecting the impact of fair value fluctuations.

operands.metric: Fair Value on Previous Reporting Date (or Initial Recognition Date)

formulas.source_formula: Net Gains from Changes in Fair Value = Fair Value on Reporting Date - Fair Value on Previous Reporting Date (or Initial Recognition Date)

nodes.name: Net Gains on Fair Value Changes
Net Growth Rate
nodes.definition: Net growth rate measures the percentage change in total subscribers after accounting for both new acquisitions and losses during a period, indicating whether a customer base is expanding or contracting.

formulas.source_formula: Net Growth Rate = Growth Rate - Churn Rate
Net Identifiable Assets = Identifiable Assets Value - Liabilities Value
Net Impact = (Coupon New - Coupon Current) - Market Conditions Change

nodes.name: Net Income
nodes.definition: Net profit refers to the net income realized by an enterprise during a specific accounting period, derived by subtracting total costs, expenses, and income tax from total revenue. It is a key financial indicator for measuring a company's operating efficiency and profitability.

formulas.source_formula: Net Profit = Total Profit - Income Tax Expense
Net Profit = Total Profit × (1 - Income Tax Rate)
Net Income = Total Revenue - Total Expenditure
Net Profit = Total Intrinsic Value - Total Premium
Net Income = Total Revenue - Total Cost - Total Expenses

nodes.name: Net Income After Tax
nodes.definition: Net income after tax, also known as net profit, refers to the final operating result of an enterprise within a specific accounting period, calculated as total profit minus income tax expense. It is a core indicator for measuring corporate profitability, conducting profit distribution, and evaluating stock value.

formulas.source_formula: Net Income After Tax = Total Profit - Income Tax Expense
Net Income After Tax = Total Profit × (1 - Income Tax Rate)

nodes.name: Net Income After Taxes (NIAT)
nodes.definition: Net Income After Taxes (NIAT) is the residual profit a company earns after deducting all operating expenses, interest, taxes, and other specified costs from revenue. It reflects the company's bottom-line profitability attributable to shareholders after tax obligations.

nodes.name: Net Income Attributable to Common Shareholders
Net Income Attributable to Common Shareholders Before Changes
aliases: Pre-change Net Income to Common Equity
nodes.definition: Net Income Attributable to Common Shareholders Before Changes refers to the portion of net income attributable to the company's common shareholders that has not yet undergone specific adjustments (such as adjustments for changes in capital structure like stock dividends or stock splits) and is used as the basis for calculating metrics such as earnings per share. It serves as the foundational data for calculating financial indicators like 'Basic Earnings Per Share Before Changes'.

nodes.name: Net Income Attributable to Common Shareholders for the Current Period
aliases: Net Income Attributable to Common Shareholders
Net Income Available to Common Shareholders
归属于公司普通股股东的净利润
归属于普通股股东的净利润
nodes.definition: Net income attributable to common shareholders for the current period refers to the portion of the company's net income for the period that belongs to common shareholders after deducting distribution items such as dividends allocated to preferred shareholders. It is not an original line item in financial statements but serves as the basis for calculating metrics such as earnings per share.

formulas.source_formula: Net Income Attributable to Common Shareholders for the Current Period = Net Income - Dividends Allocated to Preferred Shareholders

nodes.name: Net Income Attributable to Ordinary Shareholders
Net Income Increment from Conversion of Dilutive Potential Common Shares
Net Income Increment from Conversion of Dilutive Potential Ordinary Shares
aliases: Adjustment to Net Income for Dilutive Securities
Incremental Net Income from Assumed Conversion of Dilutive Potential Common Shares
假设转换时增加的净利润
nodes.definition: Net income increment from conversion of dilutive potential ordinary shares is an adjustment item to the net income attributable to ordinary shareholders for calculating diluted earnings per share. It involves the interest expense of dilutive potential ordinary shares already recognized in the current period, gains or expenses arising upon conversion, and the impact of related income taxes. It is calculated through other financial metrics and is not a fundamental raw data item in financial statements.

formulas.source_formula: Net Income Increment from Conversion of Dilutive Potential Ordinary Shares = Dividends on Convertible Preferred Shares

operands.metric: Weighted Average Number of Ordinary Shares Outstanding
Weighted Average Number of Additional Ordinary Shares from Assumed Conversion
Net Income Attributable to Ordinary Shareholders

formulas.source_formula: Net Income Increment from Conversion of Dilutive Potential Ordinary Shares = Diluted Earnings Per Share × (Weighted Average Number of Ordinary Shares Outstanding + Weighted Average Number of Additional Ordinary Shares from Assumed Conversion) - Net Income Attributable to Ordinary Shareholders

nodes.name: Net Income Under the Scenario
nodes.definition: Net income under the scenario refers to the final profit obtained by an enterprise or project after deducting all relevant costs, expenses, and income taxes under specific assumptions, conditions, or analytical frameworks. It is not a general accounting standard term, but rather a targeted application or adjustment of the concept of 'net income' based on specific analytical purposes (such as capital budgeting, valuation models, or specific operational scenarios).

nodes.name: Net Income from Leasing Other Assets
aliases: Net Rental Income from Other Assets
设备等资产出租净收益
非房屋资产出租净收入
nodes.definition: Net income from leasing other assets refers to the net profit remaining after deducting operating costs directly related to the leasing activity (such as depreciation, maintenance fees, taxes, etc.) from the rental income earned by an enterprise or individual through leasing assets other than real estate (e.g., equipment, vehicles, land). It is a component of property net income.

nodes.name: Net Income from Renting Other Assets
Net Income in Upside Scenario
nodes.definition: Net income in an upside scenario refers to the retained profit achieved by an enterprise within a specific period under assumed favorable market or operational conditions, i.e., total profit minus income tax expense. It is a core metric for assessing profitability under advantageous conditions.

formulas.source_formula: Net Income in Upside Scenario = Total Profit in Upside Scenario - Income Tax Expense
Net Income in Upside Scenario = Total Profit in Upside Scenario × (1 - Income Tax Rate)

nodes.name: Net Increase in Accounts Payable for the Period
aliases: 本期应付账款增加净额
nodes.definition: Net increase in accounts payable for the period refers to the net change in the total accounts payable of an enterprise during a specific accounting period. It is calculated by subtracting the accounts payable repaid or reduced during the period from the newly incurred accounts payable, reflecting the net amount of new, unpaid liabilities arising from the purchase of goods or acceptance of services during that period.

nodes.name: Net Increase in Accounts Receivable
nodes.definition: Net increase in accounts receivable refers to the difference between the ending balance and the beginning balance of the accounts receivable account on a company's balance sheet during a specific accounting period (such as a quarter or a year). It directly reflects the net change in the book value of accounts receivable during that period and serves as fundamental data for analyzing changes in a company's cash flow and working capital.

nodes.name: Net Increase in Advances from Customers
nodes.definition: Net increase in advances from customers refers to the difference between the ending balance and the beginning balance of the advances from customers account on the balance sheet over a specific accounting period (e.g., a quarter or a year). It reflects the net change in funds received in advance from customers during that period and serves as a fundamental raw data point for calculating cash flows from operating activities when preparing the statement of cash flows.

nodes.name: Net Increase in Cash and Cash Equivalents
aliases: 现金及现金等价物净变动额
现金及现金等价物净增加额
nodes.definition: Net increase in cash and cash equivalents refers to the difference between the ending balance and the beginning balance of cash and cash equivalents during a specific accounting period. It reflects the net inflow or outflow of cash and cash equivalents for the enterprise during that period and is the core summary indicator in the statement of cash flows.

formulas.source_formula: Net Increase in Cash and Cash Equivalents = Ending Balance of Cash - Beginning Balance of Cash + Ending Balance of Cash Equivalents - Beginning Balance of Cash Equivalents
supporting_source_formulas: Net Increase in Cash and Cash Equivalents = Ending Balance of Cash - Beginning Balance of Cash + Ending Balance of Cash Equivalents - Beginning Balance of Cash Equivalents

nodes.name: Net Increase in Cash and Cash Equivalents for the Period
aliases: Net Increase in Cash and Cash Equivalents
现金及现金等价物净增加额
nodes.definition: Net increase in cash and cash equivalents for the period refers to the difference between the ending balance and the beginning balance of cash and cash equivalents within a specific accounting period, reflecting the net change in broad cash during that period. This metric is the core summary item of the cash flow statement and can be calculated via two approaches: the direct method (calculation from balance sheet items) or the indirect method (aggregation of net amounts from various activities on the cash flow statement).

operands.metric: Net Cash Flow from Operating Activities
Net Cash Flow from Investing Activities
Net Cash Flow from Financing Activities
Effect of Exchange Rate Changes on Cash and Cash Equivalents

formulas.source_formula: Net Increase in Cash and Cash Equivalents for the Period = Net Cash Flow from Operating Activities + Net Cash Flow from Investing Activities + Net Cash Flow from Financing Activities + Effect of Exchange Rate Changes on Cash and Cash Equivalents
Net Increase in Cash and Cash Equivalents for the Period = Ending Balance of Cash - Beginning Balance of Cash + Ending Balance of Cash Equivalents - Beginning Balance of Cash Equivalents

nodes.name: Net Increase in Cash and Cash Equivalents in the Next Period
Net Increase in Notes Receivable
nodes.definition: Net increase in notes receivable refers to the difference between the ending balance of notes receivable and the beginning balance of notes receivable during a specific accounting period. This metric is a crucial adjustment item when preparing the statement of cash flows using the indirect method, used to reconcile net profit to net cash flow from operating activities, reflecting the impact of changes in notes receivable that did not generate cash flow on operating cash flow.

nodes.name: Net Increase in Operating Assets for Next Period
nodes.definition: Net increase in operating assets for the next period refers to the growth amount of a company's net operating assets (operating assets minus operating liabilities) relative to the base period during the forecast period. It is a key intermediate variable for calculating metrics such as net cash flow from operating activities for the next period.

operands.metric: Increase in Net Operating Long-term Assets

formulas.source_formula: Net Increase in Operating Assets for Next Period = Increase in Net Operating Long-term Assets - Increase in Operating Long-term Liabilities + Increase in Operating Working Capital
Net Increase in Operating Assets for Next Period = Increase in Operating Working Capital + Capital Expenditures - Depreciation and Amortization
Net Increase in Operating Assets for Next Period = Base Period Net Operating Assets × Growth Rate

nodes.name: Net Increase in Other Receivables
nodes.definition: Net increase in other receivables refers to the net amount by which the ending balance of the 'Other Receivables' account on the company's balance sheet exceeds its beginning balance during a specific accounting period. When preparing the statement of cash flows (indirect method), this net increase serves as an adjustment item to reconcile net profit to net cash flow from operating activities.

nodes.name: Net Increase in VAT Payable (Output Tax)

operands.metric: Output VAT for the Current Period
Input VAT Actually Credited in Current Period

formulas.source_formula: Net Increase in VAT Payable (Output Tax) = Current Period Output Tax - Current Period Deductible Input Tax

operands.metric: Current Period Actual Input Tax Credit

formulas.source_formula: Net Increase in VAT Payable (Output Tax) = (Current Period Tax-inclusive Sales ÷ (1 + Applicable Tax Rate) × Applicable Tax Rate) - Current Period Actual Input Tax Credit

operands.metric: Current Period Allowable Input Tax Credit
Current Period Input Tax Transfer-out Amount

formulas.source_formula: Net Increase in VAT Payable (Output Tax) = (Current Period Sales × Applicable Tax Rate) - (Current Period Allowable Input Tax Credit - Current Period Input Tax Transfer-out Amount)

nodes.name: Net Increase in Value-Added Tax Payable (Output Tax)
aliases: Net Increase in Output VAT Payable
Net Increase in VAT Payable on Sales
nodes.definition: Net Increase in Value-Added Tax Payable (Output Tax) reflects the net increase in the tax payable generated from business activities such as selling goods, providing taxable services or labor within a specific period, after considering relevant deductions or adjustments. It is a composite indicator, typically calculated based on the current period's output tax, and may involve adjustments for factors such as input tax credits, input tax transfers, and changes in carry-forward tax credits. It is used for analyzing financial information such as cash flow from operating activities.

nodes.name: Net Interest
nodes.definition: Net interest is a key metric for measuring the profitability of a financial institution's interest business, typically referring to net interest income or net interest margin. Net interest income is the difference between total interest income and total interest expense; net interest margin is the ratio of net interest income to average interest-earning assets, used to measure the efficiency of interest-earning assets in generating net interest income.

formulas.source_formula: Net Interest = Interest Income - Interest Expense
Net Interest = Net Interest Margin × Average Interest-Earning Assets
Net Interest = (Loan Interest Income + Interbank Income) - (Interest Expense + Interbank Expense)
Net Interest = Gross Interest - Taxes Due - Fees

nodes.name: Net Interest Expense
nodes.definition: Net interest expense is the amount of interest expense paid by a company after considering the impact of income tax, reflecting the cost of debt financing.

formulas.source_formula: Net Interest Expense = Interest Expense - Interest Income
Net Interest Expense = Interest Expense - (Loan Interest Income + Interbank Income)
Net Interest Expense = (Interest Expense + Interbank Expense) - (Loan Interest Income + Interbank Income)

nodes.name: Net Interest Income
nodes.definition: Net Interest Income (NII) refers to the difference between the revenue generated from interest-earning assets and the interest cost incurred on interest-bearing liabilities. For banks, assets typically include commercial and personal loans, mortgages, construction loans, and investment securities; liabilities primarily consist of customer deposits.

formulas.source_formula: Net Interest Income = Interest Income - Interest Expense

nodes.name: Net Interest Margin
nodes.definition: Net Interest Margin is the ratio of net interest income to the average balance of total interest-earning assets, used to measure the efficiency of financial institutions such as banks in generating net interest income from their interest-earning assets, and is a key indicator for assessing their profitability.

formulas.source_formula: Net Interest Margin = (Interest Income - Interest Expense) ÷ (Interest Income + Interest Expense)

nodes.name: Net Interest Rate Differential
nodes.definition: Net Interest Rate Differential (NIRD) is the difference between the interest rate earned on investments and the interest rate paid on borrowings, commonly used in carry trade strategies to measure potential profit from interest rate spreads.

formulas.source_formula: Net Interest Rate Differential = Investment Rate - Borrowing Rate

nodes.name: Net Interest Rate Spread
nodes.definition: Net interest rate spread is the difference between the average yield on interest-earning assets and the average cost of interest-bearing liabilities. It measures the pricing gap between asset yields and funding costs and is expressed in percentage points. Unlike Net Interest Margin, it does not incorporate volume mix or non-interest items and focuses solely on rate differentials.

formulas.source_formula: Net Interest Rate Spread = Interest-Earning Asset Rate - Interest-Bearing Liability Rate

nodes.name: Net Internal Rate of Return
nodes.definition: Net Internal Rate of Return (Net IRR) is the internal rate of return on an investment after adjusting cash inflows for fees and carried interest, representing the net, money-weighted annualized return to investors.

nodes.name: Net International Investment Position (NIIP)
nodes.definition: Net International Investment Position represents the stock difference between a nation's external financial assets and its external financial liabilities (domestic assets owned by nonresidents), valued at market prices at a specific point in time. A positive NIIP indicates a net creditor position, while a negative NIIP indicates a net debtor position. It is a key indicator of external sustainability, vulnerability, and overall international financial standing.

formulas.source_formula: Net International Investment Position = Foreign Assets Held - Domestic Assets Owned by Foreigners

nodes.name: Net Investment
nodes.definition: Net investment refers to the capital expenditures made by an enterprise to maintain or expand its operations, such as the purchase of fixed assets and intangible assets. It is a composite metric, calculated by the formula 'Net Investment = Capital Expenditures - Depreciation and Amortization', and is commonly used in equity cash flow analysis.

formulas.source_formula: Net Investment = Capital Expenditures - Depreciation and Amortization

nodes.name: Net Investment Amount
nodes.definition: Net investment amount is the portion of the initial investment that is actually used to purchase fund shares after deducting the front-end load fee.

formulas.source_formula: Net Investment Amount = Investment Amount - Front-End Load

nodes.name: Net Investment Borne by the Entity
Net Investment Income
nodes.definition: Net investment income refers to the net gain derived from investment activities, typically calculated as the balance of total investment income minus related investment costs and expenses. It is used to measure the profitability and efficiency of investment projects and is frequently referenced in financial analysis for the calculation of pre-tax operating profit.

formulas.source_formula: Net Investment Income = Total Investment Income - Total Investment Expenses
Net Investment Income = Dividend Income + Interest Income + Realized Capital Gains - Investment Management Fees - Transaction Costs
Net Investment Income = Total Investment Income - Total Related Expenses
Net Investment Income = Investment Revenue - Investment Expenditure
Net Investment Income = Interest and Dividends - (Accrued Expenses - Reimbursements)

nodes.name: Net Investment Income Tax
aliases: 3.8% Medicare Surtax on Net Investment Income
nodes.definition: The Net Investment Income Tax (NIIT) is a 3.8% surtax imposed on the lesser of an individual's, estate's, or trust's net investment income or the amount by which Modified Adjusted Gross Income (MAGI) exceeds applicable thresholds, designed to tax passive investment income above certain income levels.

nodes.name: Net Investment Loss
nodes.definition: Net investment loss refers to the deficit that occurs when the total expenditures (including costs, expenses, and losses) from investment activities by an enterprise or individual exceed the total income (including returns and gains) within a specific accounting period. It is a negative indicator measuring the final financial outcome of investment activities.

formulas.source_formula: Net Investment Loss = Investment Cost + Investment-related Expenses + Investment Impairment Loss - Investment Returns - Investment Disposal Gains

nodes.name: Net Investment Required to be Borne by the Entity
nodes.definition: Net investment required to be borne by the entity refers to the net increase in net operating assets (the sum of operating working capital and operating long-term assets minus operating long-term liabilities) during a specific period for maintaining or expanding the business scale, and is a key component in calculating entity free cash flow.

formulas.source_formula: Net Investment Required to be Borne by the Entity = Increase in Net Operating Assets

nodes.name: Net Investment This Year
nodes.definition: Net investment this year refers to the new net capital investment made by an enterprise in the current accounting year, typically reflected as the increase in net operating assets or capital expenditures minus depreciation and amortization. It is a key composite indicator for calculating next-period equity cash flows, rather than an original accounting statement item.

formulas.source_formula: Net Investment This Year = Increase in Net Operating Assets
Net Investment This Year = Capital Expenditures - Depreciation and Amortization
Net Investment This Year = Capital Expenditures - Depreciation + Increase in Operating Working Capital

nodes.name: Net Investment in Current Period
nodes.definition: Net investment in the current period refers to the portion of capital expenditure actually invested by an enterprise during the period, remaining after deducting depreciation and amortization, representing the new long-term capital investment of the enterprise.

formulas.source_formula: Net Investment in Current Period = Ending Net Operating Assets - Beginning Net Operating Assets
Net Investment in Current Period = Increase in Operating Working Capital + Capital Expenditure - Depreciation
Net Investment in Current Period = (Ending Net Debt + Ending Shareholders' Equity) - (Beginning Net Debt + Beginning Shareholders' Equity)

nodes.name: Net Investment in Equity Per Share for the Current Year
aliases: Net Investment per Share for Equity
nodes.definition: Net investment in equity per share for the current year refers to the net increase in shareholders' equity per share during the year, reflecting the portion of equity used for reinvestment. It is a composite metric, typically derived from fundamental data such as capital expenditure per share and the increase in working capital per share, and is used to calculate equity free cash flow per share.

operands.metric: Increase in Shareholders' Equity Per Share

formulas.source_formula: Net Investment in Equity Per Share for the Current Year = Increase in Shareholders' Equity Per Share

operands.metric: Increase in Net Operating Assets Per Share

formulas.source_formula: Net Investment in Equity Per Share for the Current Year = Increase in Net Operating Assets Per Share × (1 - Net Debt ÷ Net Operating Assets)

operands.metric: Increase in Operating Working Capital per Share

formulas.source_formula: Net Investment in Equity Per Share for the Current Year = (Increase in Operating Working Capital Per Share + Capital Expenditure Per Share - Depreciation and Amortization Per Share) × (1 - Net Debt ÷ Net Operating Assets)

nodes.name: Net Investment in Net Operating Assets in the First Year of the Continuing Period
aliases: Net Investment in Operating Assets in the First Year of the Subsequent Period
nodes.definition: Net investment in net operating assets in the first year of the continuing period refers to the increase in net operating assets invested by a company to support business growth in the first year after entering the stable growth stage (continuing period). It is a key component in calculating the entity free cash flow for the first year of the continuing period, reflecting the company's capital investment needs at the beginning of the stable growth phase.

operands.metric: Beginning Net Operating Assets in the First Year of the Continuing Period

formulas.source_formula: Net Investment in Net Operating Assets in the First Year of the Continuing Period = Beginning Net Operating Assets in the First Year of the Continuing Period × Continuing Period Growth Rate

nodes.name: Net Investment in Operating Assets
nodes.definition: Net investment in operating assets refers to the increase in a company's net operating assets, calculated as the difference between ending net operating assets and beginning net operating assets. It is a composite metric used to measure changes in investment in operating assets and is commonly applied in calculating next-period equity cash flows.

formulas.source_formula: Net Investment in Operating Assets = Beginning Net Operating Assets × Net Operating Assets Growth Rate
Net Investment in Operating Assets = Ending Net Operating Assets - Beginning Net Operating Assets

nodes.name: Net Investment in Working Capital in the Final Period of the Forecast Horizon
Net Leverage Ratio
nodes.definition: The net leverage ratio measures an insurance company's exposure to pricing, reserving, and estimation risk by comparing net premiums written plus net liabilities to policyholders' surplus. It excludes the effects of ceded reinsurance, providing a clearer view of capital adequacy and true leverage relative to surplus. A lower ratio indicates stronger capitalization and lower leverage.

formulas.source_formula: Net Leverage Ratio = (Net Premiums Written + Net Liabilities) ÷ Policyholders' Surplus

nodes.name: Net Liquid Assets
nodes.definition: Net liquid assets represent the excess of liquid assets over current liabilities, indicating a company's immediate capacity to meet short-term obligations. Liquid assets typically include cash, marketable securities, and accounts receivable, while current liabilities encompass accounts payable, accrued expenses, and the current portion of long-term debt. This measure excludes non-liquid items such as inventory and long-term assets.

formulas.source_formula: Net Liquid Assets = Liquid Assets - Current Liabilities

nodes.name: Net Loan Proceeds
nodes.definition: Net loan proceeds represent the amount disbursed to the borrower after accounting for origination fees. If the origination fee is paid upfront, the net proceeds equal the gross loan amount; if the fee is financed or withheld at disbursement, the net proceeds are reduced by the origination fee.

formulas.source_formula: Adjusted Loan Amount = Loan Amount + Origination Fee
Net Loan Proceeds = Loan Amount - Origination Fee × (1 - Fee Paid Upfront Indicator)
Net Long-Term Gain/Loss = Long-Term Capital Gains - Long-Term Capital Losses

nodes.name: Net Long-term Assets
nodes.definition: Net long-term assets refer to the net amount of a company's total long-term assets after deducting relevant impairment provisions or specific long-term liabilities. It reflects the actual value of the company's long-term assets and serves as the basis for calculating metrics such as total invested capital.

formulas.source_formula: Net Long-term Assets = Total Long-term Assets - Long-term Assets Impairment Provision

nodes.name: Net Loss
nodes.definition: Net loss is the amount by which total expenses exceed total revenues over a reporting period. It represents a negative bottom-line result on the income statement and indicates that the entity's costs and expenses surpassed its income for that period.

formulas.source_formula: Net Loss = Total Expenses - Total Revenues

nodes.name: Net Material Consumption
nodes.definition: Net material consumption refers to the quantity of materials directly required to constitute the final engineering entity or product entity in construction projects or production processes, excluding unavoidable losses and waste generated during transportation, processing, and operations at the construction or production site.

nodes.name: Net National Product
aliases: Net National Product at Market Prices
nodes.definition: Net National Product (NNP) is the total market value of final goods and services produced by a nation’s residents (GNP) minus depreciation (consumption of fixed capital). It measures the economy’s net output attributable to nationals after accounting for the wear and tear of capital assets.

formulas.source_formula: Net National Product = Gross National Product - Depreciation
Net National Product = Market Value of Goods + Market Value of Services - Depreciation

nodes.name: Net Operating Asset Increase
nodes.definition: Net operating asset increase refers to the change in net operating assets over a specific period, reflecting the net investment made to support the growth of operating activities. It is a key intermediate variable for calculating free cash flow to the firm and assessing value creation.

formulas.source_formula: Net Operating Asset Increase = Base Period Net Operating Assets × Growth Rate
Net Operating Asset Increase = Increase in Operating Working Capital + Capital Expenditures - Depreciation and Amortization

nodes.name: Net Operating Asset Investment
aliases: Net Investment in Net Operating Assets
nodes.definition: Net operating asset investment refers to the net amount invested in net operating assets (operating assets minus operating liabilities) by an enterprise during a specific period to maintain or expand its operating scale. It reflects the actual new capital employed to support business operations and serves as a key intermediate variable in calculating equity cash flows and forecasting period entity cash flows.

formulas.source_formula: Net Operating Asset Investment = Current Period Net Operating Assets - Prior Period Net Operating Assets
Net Operating Asset Investment = Gross Investment in Operating Assets - Depreciation and Amortization

nodes.name: Net Operating Asset Sales Revenue
aliases: 净经营资产对应的销售收入
经营资产净额销售收入
nodes.definition: Net Operating Asset Sales Revenue refers to the operating revenue generated by a company within a specific period through the utilization of its net operating assets (operating assets minus operating liabilities). It is a key component for calculating efficiency metrics such as the Net Operating Asset Sales Percentage, reflecting the company's ability to generate revenue using its net operating assets.

formulas.source_formula: Net Operating Asset Sales Revenue = Operating Revenue
Net Operating Asset Sales Revenue = Net Operating Assets × Net Operating Asset Turnover

nodes.name: Net Operating Asset Total Investment
aliases: Total Investment in Net Operating Assets
nodes.definition: Net operating asset total investment refers to the total capital investment made by an enterprise in operating assets within a specific period (usually an accounting period) to maintain and expand its normal business operations. It reflects the total capital scale invested by the enterprise in its operating activities and serves as the basis for calculating net operating asset net investment.

nodes.name: Net Operating Asset Turnover
nodes.definition: Net Operating Asset Turnover is the ratio of sales revenue to average net operating assets, used to measure the operating efficiency of a company's net operating assets and reflect its ability to generate sales revenue using net operating assets; a higher value indicates faster asset turnover and higher operating efficiency.

formulas.source_formula: Net Operating Asset Turnover = Sales Revenue ÷ Average Net Operating Assets
Net Operating Asset Turnover = Sales Revenue ÷ [(Beginning Net Operating Assets + Ending Net Operating Assets) ÷ 2]

nodes.name: Net Operating Asset Turnover Ratio
nodes.definition: The Net Operating Asset Turnover Ratio is a financial metric that measures the efficiency with which a company utilizes its net operating assets (operating assets minus operating liabilities) to generate sales revenue. A higher ratio generally indicates higher operational efficiency of assets, enabling the company to generate more sales revenue with less investment in net operating assets.

nodes.name: Net Operating Assets
nodes.definition: Net operating assets refer to the net value of assets used in business operations minus corresponding operating liabilities, reflecting the actual scale of funds invested in operations and serving as a key indicator for measuring business efficiency.

formulas.source_formula: Net Operating Assets = Operating Working Capital + Net Operating Long-term Assets
Net Operating Assets = Operating Assets - Operating Liabilities
Net Operating Assets = Net Debt + Owners' Equity
Net Operating Assets = Long-term Capital - Long-term Assets
Net Operating Assets = Total Assets - Non-current Assets - (Total Assets - Shareholders' Equity - Non-current Liabilities)

nodes.name: Net Operating Assets Ending Balance
aliases: 净经营营运资产期末余额
经营性净资产期末余额
nodes.definition: Net Operating Assets Ending Balance refers to the difference between a company's operating assets and operating liabilities at the balance sheet date. It represents the net capital scale actually invested in business operations and serves as the basis for calculating metrics such as net investment for the current year.

formulas.source_formula: Net Operating Assets Ending Balance = Operating Assets Ending Balance - Operating Liabilities Ending Balance

nodes.name: Net Operating Assets Growth Rate
nodes.definition: The Net Operating Assets Growth Rate is the ratio of the increase in a company's net operating assets (or net assets) during the current period to the total net operating assets (or net assets) at the end of the previous period. It reflects the expansion speed of the company's capital scale and is an important financial indicator for measuring the company's growth and sustainable development capability.

formulas.source_formula: Net Operating Assets Growth Rate = (Ending Net Operating Assets - Beginning Net Operating Assets) ÷ Beginning Net Operating Assets × 100%

nodes.name: Net Operating Assets Profit Margin
nodes.definition: Net Operating Assets Profit Margin is a key financial metric that measures a company's operational efficiency and profitability. It indicates the after-tax operating net profit generated per unit of net operating assets. As a core indicator in the enhanced DuPont analysis system, it is used to evaluate the contribution of operating activities to Return on Equity (ROE).

formulas.source_formula: Net Operating Assets Profit Margin = After-tax Operating Profit ÷ Average Net Operating Assets

nodes.name: Net Operating Assets Sales Percentage
nodes.definition: Net Operating Assets Sales Percentage refers to the percentage of revenue obtained from selling net operating assets relative to their total value, used to measure the sales efficiency and profitability of net operating assets.

formulas.source_formula: Net Operating Assets Sales Percentage = Net Operating Assets Sales Revenue ÷ Total Net Operating Assets

nodes.name: Net Operating Assets at Period Beginning
Net Operating Assets at Period End
aliases: Net Operating Assets at End of Period
nodes.definition: Net Operating Assets at Period End refers to the balance of operating assets minus operating liabilities at a specific point in time (e.g., period-end). It is a composite metric that reflects the scale of a company's operating net assets at that point and is commonly used in calculating financial analysis indicators such as the increase in net operating assets.

formulas.source_formula: Net Operating Assets at Period End = Operating Assets at Period End - Operating Liabilities at Period End

operands.metric: Net Operating Assets at Period Beginning

formulas.source_formula: Net Operating Assets at Period End = 2 × Average Net Operating Assets - Net Operating Assets at Period Beginning

nodes.name: Net Operating Assets at the Beginning of the First Year of the Continuing Period
aliases: Initial NOA of the Terminal Period
永续期首年初净经营资产
稳定增长期起点净经营资产
nodes.definition: Net Operating Assets at the beginning of the first year of the continuing period refers to the value of net operating assets at the start of the first year of the stable growth phase (i.e., the continuing or perpetual period), which coincides with the end of the final year of the forecast period, in business valuation. It serves as a critical baseline for calculating the free cash flow of the continuing period and discounting the terminal value.

nodes.name: Net Operating Assets at the End of the First Year of the Continuing Period
aliases: Ending NOA of First Year in Terminal Period
Net Operating Assets at the End of First Year in Continuing Period
后续期首年末净经营资产
永续期第一年末净经营资产
稳定期第一年末净经营资产
nodes.definition: Net Operating Assets at the end of the first year of the continuing period refers to the value of net operating assets at the end of the first year when the forecast period ends and the company enters the stable growth stage (i.e., the continuing or perpetual period) in business valuation. It is a key foundational data point for calculating the continuing period cash flows and company value.

nodes.name: Net Operating Assets for the Current Period
nodes.definition: Net operating assets for the current period refer to the net value of assets used for core business operations (excluding financial investment activities) within the current accounting period. It equals operating assets minus operating liabilities, reflecting the scale of the company's own capital actually invested in operating activities.

nodes.name: Net Operating Assets to Sales Percentage
Net Operating Cash Flow
aliases: Net Cash Flow from Operating Activities
经营活动现金流量净额
nodes.definition: Net operating cash flow is the result of gross operating cash flow minus the increase in operating working capital, reflecting the actual discretionary operating cash flow available to the enterprise without considering investment activities.

operands.metric: Total Cash Inflow from Operating Activities
Total Cash Outflows from Operating Activities

formulas.source_formula: Net Operating Cash Flow = Total Cash Inflows from Operating Activities - Total Cash Outflows from Operating Activities

nodes.name: Net Operating Income
nodes.definition: Net Operating Income is the net earnings derived from a company's core business activities after deducting all operating-related costs, expenses, and taxes. It is used to measure the profitability of core operations and serves as a key indicator in financial analysis for evaluating operating performance and solvency.

formulas.source_formula: Net Operating Income = Operating Profit × (1 - Income Tax Rate)
Net Operating Income = Net Profit - Non-operating Net Profit
supporting_source_formulas: Net Operating Income = Net Profit - Non-operating Net Profit

formulas.source_formula: Net Operating Income = Total Revenue - Operating Expenses
Net Operating Income = Gross Income - Operating Expenses
Net Operating Income = Operating Revenue + Other Business Revenue - Sales Discounts or Allowances
Net Operating Income = EBIT - Non-operating Profit + Non-operating Expenses
Net Operating Income = Sales Revenue - Sales Returns - Sales Discounts - Sales Allowances

Net Operating Income = Operating Revenue - Cost of Goods Sold - Business Taxes and Surcharges - Selling Expenses - Administrative Expenses - Research and Development Expenses - Financial Expenses - Income Tax Expense

nodes.name: Net Operating Long-term Assets
nodes.definition: Net operating long-term assets represent the net amount of long-term assets used in a company's operating activities, calculated as operating long-term assets minus operating long-term liabilities. It is a component of total net operating assets and is used to measure the net investment in a company's long-term operating assets.

nodes.name: Net Operating Long-term Assets at Period Beginning
Net Operating Long-term Assets at Period End
nodes.definition: Net operating long-term assets at period end refer to the net value of assets held by an enterprise at the end of a period that are used to support the long-term operations of its main business. Their value equals the net value of operating long-term assets at period end minus operating long-term liabilities at period end. This metric reflects the scale of net capital invested by the enterprise to sustain its long-term operating activities and is a key component in calculating net operating assets at period end.

operands.metric: Net Value of Operating Long-term Assets at Period End
Operating Long-term Liabilities at Period End

formulas.source_formula: Net Operating Long-term Assets at Period End = Net Value of Operating Long-term Assets at Period End - Operating Long-term Liabilities at Period End

operands.metric: Original Value of Operating Long-term Assets

formulas.source_formula: Net Operating Long-term Assets at Period End = Original Value of Operating Long-term Assets - Accumulated Depreciation and Amortization

operands.metric: Net Operating Long-term Assets at Period Beginning
Increase in Net Value of Operating Long-term Assets during the Period
Increase in Operating Long-term Liabilities during the Period

formulas.source_formula: Net Operating Long-term Assets at Period End = Net Operating Long-term Assets at Period Beginning + Increase in Net Value of Operating Long-term Assets during the Period - Increase in Operating Long-term Liabilities during the Period

nodes.name: Net Operating Profit
nodes.definition: Net Operating Profit, also known as Net Operating Profit After Tax (NOPAT), refers to the after-tax profit generated from a company's core business activities, reflecting the after-tax profitability of its operations. It is calculated by adjusting operating profit or operating revenue and serves as a crucial basis for calculating financial ratios such as Return on Net Operating Assets.

nodes.name: Net Operating Profit After Tax
nodes.definition: Net Operating Profit After Tax (NOPAT) refers to the after-tax profit generated from a company's operating activities, excluding the impact of capital structure. It reflects the profitability of the company's assets and is a key metric in free cash flow calculation and financial analysis.

formulas.source_formula: Net Operating Profit After Tax = Operating Profit × (1 - Income Tax Rate)
Net Operating Profit After Tax = Earnings Before Interest and Taxes × (1 - Income Tax Rate)
Net Operating Profit After Tax = Total Profit - Income Tax Expense
Net Operating Profit After Tax (NOPAT) = Operating Profit × (1 - Effective Tax Rate)
Net Operating Profit After Tax (NOPAT) = Operating Income (EBIT) × (1 - Tax Rate)
Net Operating Profit After Tax = Sales Revenue - Operating Expenses - Income Tax
Net Operating Profit After Tax = Net Profit + (Interest Expense + R&D Expense Adjustment - Non-recurring Income Adjustment) × (1 - Income Tax Rate)

nodes.name: Net Operating Profit Less Adjusted Taxes (NOPLAT)
aliases: Net Operating Profit Less Adjusted Taxes
净营业利润（扣除调整后税项）
扣除调整税项后的经营利润
nodes.definition: Net Operating Profit Less Adjusted Taxes (NOPLAT) is the after-tax operating profit generated from a company’s core operations, independent of capital structure. It applies the effective tax rate to operating income (EBIT) to reflect operating efficiency and is widely used in DCF valuation, EVA, and performance measurement.

nodes.name: Net Operating Revenue
nodes.definition: Net operating revenue refers to the net amount derived from total operating revenue after deducting sales discounts and allowances from activities such as selling goods and providing services in daily business operations. It is a key metric for measuring the scale of a company's core business income and is commonly used in calculating efficiency ratios such as asset turnover.

formulas.source_formula: Net Operating Revenue = Operating Revenue + Other Operating Revenue - Sales Discounts or Allowances
supporting_source_formulas: Net Operating Revenue = Operating Revenue + Other Operating Revenue - Sales Discounts or Allowances

formulas.source_formula: Net Ordinary Gain = Ordinary Income - Ordinary Expenses
Net Overall Gain = Net Ordinary Gain + Capital Deduction

nodes.name: Net Pay
nodes.definition: Net pay is the amount an employee receives after all payroll deductions are subtracted from gross pay, including pre-tax deductions, FICA taxes (Social Security and Medicare), income taxes, and voluntary deductions.

formulas.source_formula: Net Payment = Receivables - Payables
Net Payment = 0
Net Payment = (Current Rate − Ceiling Rate) × Notional Amount
Net Payment = (Floor Rate − Current Rate) × Notional Amount
Net Payment (Total Return Swap) = Principal × (Reference Asset Return - Set Rate)
Net Payment USD = Interest Payment USD - (Interest Payment Foreign ÷ Exchange Rate)

nodes.name: Net Premium
nodes.definition: Net premium is an actuarial measure of premium that excludes expenses and loadings. In this context, it is computed as the difference between the present value of policy benefits and the present value of future premiums, reflecting the net amount attributable to benefits after considering future premium inflows.

formulas.source_formula: Net Premium = Present Value of Benefits - Present Value of Future Premiums

nodes.name: Net Premiums Written
nodes.definition: Net premiums written represent the amount of premiums an insurer retains for risk after ceding a portion to reinsurers and adding premiums assumed from other insurers within a period. It reflects underwriting volume and risk retention and differs from net premiums earned, which recognizes the portion of written premiums attributable to the elapsed coverage period.

formulas.source_formula: Net Premiums Written = Premiums Written - Premiums Ceded + Reinsurance Assumed

nodes.name: Net Present Value
nodes.definition: Net Present Value is the difference between the present value of future cash flows discounted at a specified rate and the initial investment amount. It is used to evaluate the financial feasibility and profitability of investment projects and is a core composite indicator in capital budgeting.

operands.metric: Present Value of Future Net Cash Flows
Present Value of Original Investment Amount

formulas.source_formula: Net Present Value = Present Value of Future Net Cash Flows - Present Value of Original Investment Amount

operands.metric: Present Value of Residual Value Inflows

formulas.source_formula: Net Present Value = Present Value of Rental Inflows + Present Value of Residual Value Inflows - Acquisition Cost

nodes.name: Net Present Value (Absolute Value)
nodes.definition: Net Present Value (absolute value) is the difference between the present value of a project's future net cash flows discounted at a predetermined rate and the present value of the initial investment, used to assess the financial feasibility of an investment project. An NPV greater than zero indicates that the project's rate of return exceeds the discount rate, making the project viable.

operands.metric: Present Value of Future Net Cash Flows

formulas.source_formula: Net Present Value (Absolute Value) = Present Value of Future Net Cash Flows - Present Value of Original Investment

nodes.name: Net Present Value (Lessee)
nodes.definition: Net Present Value (Lessee) is the value used by a lessee in lease decision-making, assessed by comparing the asset acquisition cost against the difference between the present value of cash inflows from leasing and the present value of the terminal asset.

operands.metric: Present Value of Lease Period Cash Flows

formulas.source_formula: Net Present Value (Lessee) = Asset Acquisition Cost - Present Value of Lease Period Cash Flows - Present Value of Terminal Asset

nodes.name: Net Present Value (Lessor)
nodes.definition: Net Present Value (Lessor) is the net value of the present value of after-tax cash inflows from leasing activities and the present value of the end-of-term asset, minus the asset acquisition cost.

nodes.name: Net Present Value Rule
nodes.definition: The Net Present Value (NPV) Rule is a capital budgeting decision criterion that evaluates an investment by discounting expected future cash inflows at the cost of capital to obtain their present value and subtracting the initial investment. Projects with NPV > 0 are expected to create shareholder value and should be accepted, while those with NPV < 0 should be rejected.

nodes.name: Net Present Value of Finance Lease (Lessee)
aliases: Net Present Value of Finance Lease for Lessee
nodes.definition: Net Present Value of Finance Lease (Lessee) is a net benefit indicator calculated by the lessee under a finance lease arrangement, comparing the cost of the leased asset with the present value of after-tax cash flows during the lease term and the present value of the terminal asset. It is used to assess the feasibility of the leasing decision.

operands.metric: Present Value of After-Tax Cash Flows During Lease Term

formulas.source_formula: Net Present Value of Finance Lease (Lessee) = Cost of Leased Asset - Present Value of After-Tax Cash Flows during Lease Term - Present Value of Terminal Asset

nodes.name: Net Present Value of Growth Opportunities (NPVGO)
aliases: Net Present Value of Growth Opportunities
nodes.definition: Net Present Value of Growth Opportunities (NPVGO) measures the incremental value created by undertaking growth projects, calculated as the present value of projected cash inflows discounted at the cost of capital minus the initial investment.

formulas.source_formula: Net Present Value of Growth Opportunities (NPVGO) = Discounted Cash Flows - Initial Investment

nodes.name: Net Present Value of Growth Opportunities (Per Share)

operands.metric: Expected Earnings per Share from Growth Opportunities

formulas.source_formula: Net Present Value of Growth Opportunities (Per Share) = Expected Earnings per Share from Growth Opportunities ÷ (Discount Rate - Growth Rate)

nodes.name: Net Present Value under Risk-Adjusted Discount Rate Method
aliases: 风险调整折现率法净现值
nodes.definition: Net Present Value under the risk-adjusted discount rate method discounts expected cash flows at a rate that includes a risk premium to reflect the risk level of the project.

nodes.name: Net Proceeds
nodes.definition: Net proceeds represent the cash amount received from the sale of an asset after deducting all transaction-related costs, such as brokerage fees, commissions, advertising costs, closing costs, and taxes. It reflects the final cash inflow attributable to the sale.

formulas.source_formula: Net Proceeds = Gross Proceeds - Total Costs

nodes.name: Net Proceeds from Bond Issuance
