It reflects the total assets owned by the enterprise at the beginning of the period that are expected to be realized or consumed within a normal operating cycle (typically one year or an operating cycle longer than one year). This figure serves as fundamental data for analyzing the enterprise's short-term solvency and working capital position.

nodes.name: Total Current Assets at Period End
nodes.definition: Total current assets at period end refers to the aggregate value of all assets owned by an enterprise at the accounting period end (e.g., balance sheet date) that are expected to be realized, sold, or consumed within one normal operating cycle or one year (whichever is longer). It is a composite indicator calculated by summing multiple basic accounting items, used to measure the enterprise's short-term solvency and working capital position.

formulas.source_formula: Total Current Assets at Period End = Cash and Cash Equivalents + Net Accounts Receivable + Inventory

operands.metric: Non-current Assets Due within One Year

formulas.source_formula: Total Current Assets at Period End = Cash and Cash Equivalents + Notes Receivable + Accounts Receivable + Other Receivables + Inventory + Prepaid Expenses + Non-current Assets Due Within One Year

nodes.name: Total Current Assets of Previous Period
nodes.definition: Total Current Assets of Previous Period refers to the aggregate value of all assets owned by an enterprise during the previous accounting period (e.g., the previous fiscal year or the end of the previous accounting period) that are expected to be realized, sold, or consumed within one normal operating cycle or one year (whichever is longer). It is a composite metric calculated by summing the balances of various current asset accounts from the previous period according to specific formulas, primarily used for trend comparison and metric calculation in financial analysis, such as determining the operating current assets of the previous period.

operands.metric: Cash and Cash Equivalents of Previous Period
Net Accounts Receivable of Previous Period

formulas.source_formula: Total Current Assets of Previous Period = Cash and Cash Equivalents of Previous Period + Net Accounts Receivable of Previous Period + Inventory of Previous Period

operands.metric: Cash and Cash Equivalents of Previous Period
Non-current Assets Due within One Year (Previous Period)

formulas.source_formula: Total Current Assets of Previous Period = Cash and Cash Equivalents of Previous Period + Notes Receivable of Previous Period + Accounts Receivable of Previous Period + Other Receivables of Previous Period + Inventory of Previous Period + Prepaid Expenses of Previous Period + Non-current Assets Due Within One Year of Previous Period

nodes.name: Total Current Liabilities
nodes.definition: Total current liabilities refer to the aggregate amount of debt that a company must repay within one year or one operating cycle. It is a composite indicator derived from the summation of various short-term liability items and serves as a key financial metric for assessing a company's short-term solvency and working capital management.

formulas.source_formula: Total Current Liabilities = Short-term Borrowings + Notes Payable + Accounts Payable + Advances from Customers + Employee Benefits Payable + Taxes Payable + Interest Payable + Dividends Payable + Other Payables + Current Portion of Non-current Liabilities + Other Current Liabilities

Total Current Liabilities = Short-term Borrowings + Accounts Payable + Advances from Customers + Employee Benefits Payable + Taxes Payable + Other Payables + Current Portion of Long-term Debt + Other Current Liabilities

nodes.name: Total Current Liabilities at Beginning of Period
nodes.definition: Total current liabilities at the beginning of the period refers to the aggregate balance of all debt items on the balance sheet that are due for repayment within one year or one operating cycle, as recorded at the start of a specific accounting period (such as a fiscal year or quarter). This figure is directly sourced from the company's accounting records or financial statements and serves as fundamental data reflecting the enterprise's short-term debt repayment pressure at the period's commencement.

nodes.name: Total Current Liabilities for the Period
nodes.definition: Total current liabilities for the period refer to the aggregate sum of all debts that a company is obligated to repay within one year or within one normal operating cycle (whichever is longer) as of the end of the current accounting period (e.g., the current quarter or fiscal year). It reflects the company's short-term debt repayment pressure.

nodes.name: Total Current Liabilities of Previous Period
nodes.definition: Total current liabilities of the previous period refers to the aggregate book value of all debts that an enterprise is obligated to repay within a normal operating cycle (typically one year or one operating cycle longer than a year) at the end of the preceding accounting period (such as the previous fiscal year, quarter, or month).

nodes.name: Total Current Period Long-term Operating Liabilities
nodes.definition: Total Current Period Long-term Operating Liabilities refers to the aggregate amount of liabilities arising from daily business operations (such as procurement, production, and sales) with repayment terms exceeding one year, as of the end of the current accounting period (e.g., the current fiscal year or quarter). It reflects the scale of debt that a company has undertaken to support its long-term operations and is due for repayment beyond one year in the future.

nodes.name: Total Cycle Time
nodes.definition: Total cycle time refers to the entire time span from the start to the end of a process, typically used to measure the overall time required to complete a task, process an order, or execute a business process.

nodes.name: Total Daily Cost
nodes.definition: Total Daily Cost refers to the sum of all cost expenses incurred by an enterprise in one day of production and business activities, typically including daily fixed costs and variable costs.

nodes.name: Total Daily Expenses
nodes.definition: Total daily expenses refer to the sum of all costs and expenditures incurred by a business, project, or individual within a single day, encompassing various types of expenses such as fixed costs and variable costs.

nodes.name: Total Days in Period
nodes.definition: Total Days in Period refers to the complete number of calendar days between two specific dates, derived directly from date calculations. In the accounting and finance field, it is commonly used to calculate derived metrics such as daily averages and turnover rates, serving as a fundamental input parameter for many financial analyses.

nodes.name: Total Days in Reporting Period
nodes.definition: Total days in the reporting period refers to a predetermined constant number of days used in financial calculations and analysis to standardize the time base, facilitate comparison and computation. It typically represents the length of a complete fiscal year or a specific analysis period, such as 365 days (calendar year) or 360 days (commercial year), and serves as a fundamental parameter in the calculation of many financial ratios (e.g., days turnover ratios).

nodes.name: Total Days in Year
nodes.definition: Total Days in Year is a time parameter used in financial calculations to derive other metrics (such as average daily requirements). It is typically derived through formulas, such as using a 360-day convention (30 days per month for 12 months) or determining actual calendar days based on leap year (365 or 366 days), rather than being a raw base figure from financial statements.

formulas.source_formula: Total Days in Year = 30 × 12
Total Debits = Total Credits

nodes.name: Total Debt
nodes.definition: Total debt refers to the present obligations arising from past transactions or events of an enterprise, the fulfillment of which is expected to result in an outflow of economic benefits from the enterprise. It includes both current liabilities and non-current liabilities, representing the aggregate of the enterprise's liabilities, and reflects its financial leverage and debt repayment capacity.

formulas.source_formula: Total Debt = Total Assets - Total Equity
Total Debt = Total Liabilities + External Claims
Total Debt = Current Liabilities + Non-current Liabilities

nodes.name: Total Debt Financing
nodes.definition: Total Debt Financing refers to the total amount of funds raised by a company through debt instruments, representing the net debt financing scale after adjusting for cash and cash equivalents. It is commonly used in financial analysis such as debt cost of capital and capital structure management.

nodes.name: Total Debt Service
nodes.definition: Total Debt Service refers to the aggregate cash outflow required by a company to fulfill all debt obligations within a specific period (typically one year). It is a key metric for assessing a company's debt burden and is commonly used to calculate financial indicators such as the Debt Service Coverage Ratio. As a composite calculated figure, it is typically derived by summing various mandatory debt payments, including interest expense, principal repayments, sinking fund payments, and lease payments, rather than being directly obtained from a single line item on financial statements.

formulas.source_formula: Total Debt Service = Interest Expense + Principal Repayment + Sinking Fund Payment + Lease Payment

nodes.name: Total Debt Service Ratio
nodes.definition: The Total Debt Service (TDS) ratio measures a borrower's total monthly debt obligations relative to gross monthly income, expressed as a percentage. Lenders use it to assess debt capacity and creditworthiness; lower ratios indicate stronger ability to service debt, with typical underwriting thresholds at or below 36–43%.

formulas.source_formula: Total Debt Service Ratio (%) = (Total Monthly Debt Obligations ÷ Gross Monthly Income) × 100

nodes.name: Total Debt at Beginning of Period
nodes.definition: Total debt at the beginning of the period refers to the total liabilities of an enterprise at the start of an accounting period, representing the total liabilities at the beginning of the period. As a non-leaf node, it can be calculated through financial indicators such as the sum of current liabilities and non-current liabilities at the beginning of the period, or the difference between total assets and total owners' equity at the beginning of the period.

nodes.name: Total Debt at Period End
nodes.definition: Total debt at period end refers to the total liabilities borne by an enterprise at the end of an accounting period, including current liabilities and non-current liabilities. It reflects the present obligations arising from past transactions or events, the fulfillment of which is expected to result in an outflow of economic benefits from the enterprise. This indicator serves as the basis for assessing solvency and capital structure in financial analysis. It is typically calculated as the sum of current liabilities and non-current liabilities, or derived from total assets minus total owners' equity at period end.

formulas.source_formula: Total Debt at Period End = Current Liabilities + Non-current Liabilities

nodes.name: Total Debt-to-Capitalization
nodes.definition: Total Debt-to-Capitalization is a leverage ratio that measures the proportion of a company's interest-bearing debt relative to total capitalization (debt plus shareholders' equity), indicating the extent to which the capital structure is financed by debt and the associated financial risk.

formulas.source_formula: Total Debt-to-Capitalization = Total Debt ÷ Total Capitalization

nodes.name: Total Debt-to-Income Ratio
nodes.definition: The Total Debt-to-Income Ratio (DTI) measures the proportion of an individual's or household's gross monthly income required to service all recurring debt obligations, including housing costs, credit cards, auto loans, and student loans. It is a key underwriting metric used by lenders to assess repayment capacity; under the 28/36 rule, the back-end DTI is generally expected to be at or below 36%.

formulas.source_formula: Total Debt-to-Income Ratio = Total Monthly Debt Payments ÷ Gross Monthly Income

nodes.name: Total Debt-to-Total Assets Ratio
nodes.definition: The total debt-to-total assets ratio measures the proportion of a company's assets financed by debt, calculated as total debt divided by total assets. It indicates leverage and long-term solvency risk.

formulas.source_formula: Total Debt-to-Total Assets Ratio = Total Debt ÷ Total Assets

nodes.name: Total Deductions
nodes.definition: Total deductions refer to the sum of various expenses, costs, losses, and other specific items that are permitted to be subtracted from an individual's or enterprise's gross income according to tax laws and relevant regulations when calculating taxable income. The purpose is to reasonably deduct necessary expenditures before taxation to determine the final taxable profit or income.

nodes.name: Total Demand
nodes.definition: Total demand refers to the aggregate quantity of goods or services demanded by society or economic entities within a specific period. In macroeconomics, it typically refers to aggregate social demand, including consumption, investment, government spending, and net exports. In financial management, it refers to the total financing demand required by a company to support its operations and growth, which can be calculated through indicators such as changes in net operating assets.

formulas.source_formula: Total Demand = Consumption Demand + Investment Demand
Total Demand = Projected Net Operating Assets - Base Period Net Operating Assets
Total Demand = Current Period Total Investment Demand + Current Period Total Consumption Demand + Current Period Total Foreign Demand
Total Demand = (Projected Operating Assets - Projected Operating Liabilities) - (Base Period Operating Assets - Base Period Operating Liabilities)

nodes.name: Total Department Variable Cost
nodes.definition: Total department variable cost refers to the sum of all costs incurred by a specific department (e.g., production department, sales department) within a given accounting period, the total amount of which changes in direct proportion to changes in the department's activity level (e.g., production volume, sales volume). Examples include direct material costs, direct labor costs, and power costs calculated based on output.

formulas.source_formula: Total Deposit = Required Funds ÷ (1 - Equity Requirement)
Total Depreciable Amount = Original Value - Salvage Value
Total Diluted Shares = Common Shares Outstanding + Potential Dilutive Shares

nodes.name: Total Direct Costs and Expenses
nodes.definition: Total direct costs and expenses refer to the sum of all costs and expenses in a company's production and operating activities that can be directly attributed to specific products or services and can be precisely traced and measured. It typically includes expenditures directly related to production, such as direct materials and direct labor.

nodes.name: Total Direct Labor Cost
nodes.definition: Total direct labor cost refers to the aggregate sum of all labor costs paid by an enterprise within a specific period for employees directly engaged in product manufacturing or providing specific services. It typically includes base wages, allowances, bonuses, benefits (such as social insurance and housing provident fund), and related training expenses, constituting a significant component of product cost.

nodes.name: Total Direct Manufacturing Overhead
nodes.definition: Total direct manufacturing overhead refers to the sum of manufacturing costs that can be directly attributed to specific cost objects (such as products, batches, or production steps) during the production process. It is typically listed alongside direct materials and direct labor as an independent basic cost item for accumulation and recording in the cost calculation sheet.

nodes.name: Total Direct Material Cost
nodes.definition: Total direct material cost refers to the aggregate cost of all raw materials directly consumed and forming the physical substance of products during a specific accounting period (such as a month or a production cycle). It is typically calculated by directly summarizing source documents such as material requisition forms and purchase invoices, serving as fundamental data for product cost accounting.

nodes.name: Total Distributable Profit
nodes.definition: Total distributable profit refers to the total profit that a company can allocate to shareholders (such as dividend payments) or retain for future development after calculation and adjustments within a specific accounting period. It typically does not equal the net profit reported in the income statement, but is derived by adding the beginning retained earnings to the net profit and considering other transfers or adjustments (such as surplus reserve covering losses).

nodes.name: Total Dividend Amount
nodes.definition: Total Dividend Amount refers to the aggregate amount of dividends paid by a company to all shareholders (including common shareholders and preferred shareholders) over a specific period. It is not a direct line item in financial statements but rather a comprehensive metric calculated using indicators such as net profit, retained earnings, or cash dividends, reflecting the company's dividend distribution policy and scale.

formulas.source_formula: Total Dividend Amount = Net Profit - Increase in Retained Earnings

nodes.name: Total Dividend Payments for the Period
aliases: Total Dividend Paid in Current Period
nodes.definition: Total dividend payments for the period refer to the aggregate amount of cash dividends actually paid by the company to its shareholders during the current accounting period (such as a quarter or a year). It reflects the scale of funds outflow used by the company to reward shareholders during that period and is typically presented in the financing activities section of the cash flow statement.

nodes.name: Total Dividends
nodes.definition: Total dividends refer to the aggregate amount of cash dividends declared and paid by a company to its shareholders during a specific accounting period, reflecting the company's profit distribution level to shareholders. It is typically calculated based on net profit, retained earnings at the beginning of the period, and various appropriation items, serving as a key indicator in dividend policy and financial statement analysis.

nodes.name: Total Dividends of Previous Year
nodes.definition: Total Dividends of Previous Year refers to the total cash dividends actually paid or declared by a company to its common shareholders during the last fiscal year. It reflects the scale of the company's profit distribution to shareholders and serves as the basis for calculating metrics such as dividends per share.

operands.metric: Appropriation to Employee Bonus and Welfare Fund

formulas.source_formula: Total Dividends of Previous Year = Net Profit + Beginning Retained Earnings - Appropriation to Surplus Reserve - Appropriation to Statutory Reserve - Appropriation to Employee Bonus and Welfare Fund - Ending Retained Earnings
Total Early Withdrawal Cost = Early Withdrawal Penalty + Income Tax on Withdrawal

nodes.name: Total Employee Benefits Payable for the Year
Total Employer Contributions
nodes.definition: Total Employer Contributions refers to the sum of all welfare payments made by an enterprise for its employees, including statutory pension insurance, medical insurance, etc. (the five social insurances and one housing fund), as well as voluntarily provided benefits such as enterprise annuities and supplementary medical insurance.

nodes.name: Total Employment Insurance (EI) Benefits
nodes.definition: Total Employment Insurance (EI) benefits represent the cumulative amount of government-provided unemployment insurance payments an eligible claimant receives over the benefit period. It is computed by multiplying the weekly EI benefit rate by the number of weeks of eligible coverage.

formulas.source_formula: Total EI Benefits = Weekly EI Benefit Rate × Duration (Weeks)

nodes.name: Total Enterprise Value (TEV)
nodes.definition: Total Enterprise Value (TEV) is a comprehensive measure of a company's total value to all capital providers. It is calculated as equity value (market capitalization) plus total debt and preferred stock, minus cash and cash equivalents. TEV facilitates comparisons across firms with different capital structures and is widely used in valuation and mergers and acquisitions to assess the implied acquisition price.

nodes.name: Total Equity Value
nodes.definition: Total equity value refers to the aggregate market value of all outstanding common shares of a company calculated at current market prices, representing the market's total valuation of shareholders' ownership of the company's net assets.

nodes.name: Total Equity at Period End
nodes.definition: Total equity at period end refers to the total residual interest owned by shareholders after deducting liabilities from assets at the end of an accounting period (e.g., month-end, quarter-end, year-end), serving as a core indicator reflecting a company's capital structure and financial strength.

formulas.source_formula: Total Equity at Period End = Paid-in Capital at Period End + Capital Reserve at Period End + Surplus Reserve at Period End + Retained Earnings at Period End

nodes.name: Total Equity at the End of the First Quarter
aliases: Total Shareholders' Equity at the End of Q1
第一季度末股东权益总额
nodes.definition: Total equity at the end of the first quarter refers to the total net assets of an enterprise attributable to its owners at the specific point in time of the first quarter's end, reflecting the enterprise's own capital strength and financial foundation.

operands.metric: Total Assets at End of First Quarter
Total Liabilities at the End of the First Quarter

formulas.source_formula: Total Equity at the End of the First Quarter = Total Assets at the End of the First Quarter - Total Liabilities at the End of the First Quarter

operands.metric: Paid-in Capital at the End of the First Quarter
Capital Reserve at the End of the First Quarter
Surplus Reserve at the End of the First Quarter
Retained Earnings at the End of the First Quarter

formulas.source_formula: Total Equity at the End of the First Quarter = Paid-in Capital at the End of the First Quarter + Capital Reserve at the End of the First Quarter + Surplus Reserve at the End of the First Quarter + Retained Earnings at the End of the First Quarter

nodes.name: Total Equity at the End of the Year Three Years Ago
aliases: Total Owner's Equity at the End of Three Years Ago
Total Shareholders' Equity at the End of the Year Three Years Prior
三年前年末净资产总额
三年前年末股东权益总额
三年前期末所有者权益
nodes.definition: Total equity at the end of the year three years ago refers to the total residual value of interests owned by the enterprise's owners (shareholders) after subtracting total liabilities from total assets at the end of the accounting year three years prior. It reflects the scale of the enterprise's own capital or net assets at that specific historical point in time and serves as a crucial historical benchmark data for calculating dynamic indicators such as capital growth rate.

nodes.name: Total Equity of Subsidiary
aliases: 子公司所有者权益总额
nodes.definition: Total equity of a subsidiary refers to the aggregate residual interest in the assets of the subsidiary, as an independent legal entity, after deducting its liabilities, which is collectively owned by the subsidiary's owners (including the controlling parent company and other minority shareholders). In consolidated financial statements, it serves as the foundational component for calculating the equity attributable to owners of the parent and minority interests.

nodes.name: Total Estimated Contract Workload
nodes.definition: Total Estimated Contract Workload refers to the pre-estimate made by management based on professional experience and technical assessment, prior to or during the execution of a construction contract, of the total workload (such as man-hours, engineering quantity, etc.) required to complete the entire contract project. It serves as a fundamental input for calculating financial metrics such as the percentage of contract completion and constitutes a significant professional judgment and initial estimate.

nodes.name: Total Estimated Dividends
nodes.definition: Total Estimated Dividends refers to the total amount of dividends that a company plans to distribute to all shareholders (typically common shareholders) over a specific future period, based on its future earnings forecasts, investment plans, capital structure, and dividend policy (such as the residual dividend policy).

nodes.name: Total Estimated Fixed Manufacturing Overhead
aliases: 固定制造费用预算总额
nodes.definition: Total Estimated Fixed Manufacturing Overhead refers to the pre-estimated total amount of manufacturing overhead costs that do not vary with the level of business activity (such as production volume or labor hours) during the budget period, incurred to maintain normal production operations. It is a crucial component in preparing comprehensive budgets, particularly the manufacturing overhead budget and product cost budget.

nodes.name: Total Estimated Standard Direct Labor Wages
Total Estimated Wages for Planned Operating Period
Total Expected Cash Inflows
nodes.definition: Total expected cash inflows refer to the total amount of cash projected to be received during a specific future period. It is the forecasted version of cash inflows, which can be calculated from expected net cash flow and expected cash outflows. It is a non-leaf node concept commonly used in financial forecasting, stress testing, and cash flow management.

nodes.name: Total Expected Cash Outflow
nodes.definition: Total Expected Cash Outflow refers to the sum of all projected cash expenditures that an enterprise or project is expected to incur during a specific forecast period. It is a composite indicator based on financial forecasts, commonly used in cash flow budgeting, project investment evaluation, and liquidity stress testing (e.g., total net cash outflow under a 30-day stress scenario), providing a critical basis for funding arrangements and solvency analysis.

formulas.source_formula: Total Expected Cash Outflow = Cash Outflow from Operating Activities + Cash Outflow from Investing Activities + Cash Outflow from Financing Activities
Total Expected Cash Outflow = Construction Investment + Working Capital + Operating Costs + Value-Added Tax Payable + Input Tax Credit + Surcharges and Fees + Maintenance and Operation Investment

nodes.name: Total Expected Dividends
nodes.definition: Total Expected Dividends refers to the sum of all cash dividends that investors or analysts anticipate a company will pay to all shareholders over a specific future period (typically one fiscal year), based on the company's historical dividend policy, earnings forecasts, cash flow position, and future development plans.

nodes.name: Total Expected Liabilities
nodes.definition: Total Expected Liabilities refers to the aggregate amount of a company's liabilities calculated based on forecasted future data, reflecting all debts the company is projected to bear at a specific future point in time. It is a composite metric derived from projected balance sheet items and serves as a crucial basis for financial forecasting, capital structure analysis, and risk assessment.

formulas.source_formula: Total Expected Liabilities = Expected Current Liabilities + Expected Non-current Liabilities

nodes.name: Total Expected Rate of Return
nodes.definition: The total expected rate of return is the anticipated overall return obtained by an investor after allocating funds between risky assets and risk-free assets.

operands.metric: Expected Rate of Return of Risky Portfolio

formulas.source_formula: Total Expected Rate of Return = Proportion Invested in Risky Portfolio × Expected Rate of Return of Risky Portfolio + (1 - Proportion Invested in Risky Portfolio) × Risk-free Rate

nodes.name: Total Expenditure
nodes.definition: Total expenditure refers to the sum of all expense items within a specific period, serving as a core financial metric for measuring cash outflows and cost consumption of an enterprise or individual. It is typically used as the basis for calculating key indicators such as net income and unit variable cost.

nodes.name: Total Expense Budget
nodes.definition: Total Expense Budget refers to the sum of all pre-planned and approved expense expenditures for various business activities within a specific budget period (typically one fiscal year) by an enterprise or organization. It encompasses major cost and expense categories such as main business costs, operating expenses, administrative expenses, and financial expenses, serving as a core indicator for cost control and financial planning.

nodes.name: Total Expense Ratio (TER)
nodes.definition: Total Expense Ratio (TER) is a cost efficiency metric for investment funds that expresses total operating expenses as a percentage of total fund assets. It typically includes management, administration, trading, and overhead costs, indicating the proportion of assets consumed by operating the fund.

formulas.source_formula: Total Expense Ratio (TER) = Total Fund Costs ÷ Total Fund Assets × 100%

nodes.name: Total Expenses
nodes.definition: Total expenses refer to the aggregate sum of all expenditures incurred by an enterprise during a specific accounting period (such as a year or a quarter) for conducting business operations, raising funds, and performing daily management activities. It typically includes major categories such as cost of goods sold, operating expenses (or selling expenses), administrative expenses, and financial expenses, serving as a crucial indicator for measuring resource consumption and cost control levels within the enterprise.

nodes.name: Total Expenses to be Allocated
nodes.definition: Total Expenses to be Allocated refers to the aggregate sum of all expenses that need to be distributed to different cost objects (such as products, departments, or projects) according to specific criteria in cost accounting or expense allocation processes. It typically represents the accumulated amount of indirect or common expenses incurred during an accounting period for production or service provision that have not yet been assigned to specific objects.

nodes.name: Total Exports of Goods and Services
nodes.definition: Total exports of goods and services refers to the aggregate market value of all goods and services sold by a country or region to the rest of the world within a specific period (typically a year or a quarter). It is a key macroeconomic indicator for measuring a country's external economic activity and international competitiveness.

nodes.name: Total FICA Tax
nodes.definition: FICA tax is the employee payroll tax withheld to fund Social Security (OASDI) and Medicare. The standard employee portion totals 7.65%, composed of 6.2% for Social Security (subject to an annual wage base limit) and 1.45% for Medicare (with an additional 0.9% surcharge for high earners not reflected here). This measure represents the total FICA withholding from an employee’s gross pay for a pay period under the standard combined rate assumption.

formulas.source_formula: Total FICA Tax = Social Security Tax + Medicare Tax + Additional Medicare Tax

nodes.name: Total Face Value of Convertible Bonds
aliases: Aggregate Par Value of Convertible Bonds
nodes.definition: Total face value of convertible bonds refers to the aggregate par value of all convertible bonds issued by a company, as set at the time of issuance. It serves as fundamental data for calculating conversion ratios, assessing potential equity dilution effects, and conducting related financial analysis.

nodes.name: Total Face Value of Debt Issued
Total Face Value of Issued Debt
aliases: Total Par Value of Debt Issued
nodes.definition: Total face value of issued debt refers to the aggregate principal amount (i.e., face value) stated on all debt instruments, such as bonds and notes, issued by a company to raise funds from investors. It represents the total principal amount of debt that the company is obligated to repay and serves as a key foundational data point for calculating metrics such as the company's total market value.

nodes.name: Total Factor Productivity
nodes.definition: Total Factor Productivity refers to the comprehensive utilization efficiency of all input factors (such as capital, labor, etc.) in the production process. It measures the ratio between total output and total factor input, reflecting the portion of economic growth attributable to technological progress, organizational innovation, scale effects, and other factors not directly explained by the quantity of factor inputs.

formulas.source_formula: Total Finance Charge = (Original Payments × Monthly Payment) - Original Loan Amount

nodes.name: Total Financial Assets
nodes.definition: Total financial assets refer to the aggregate carrying amount of all financial instruments held by an enterprise at a specific point in time (e.g., the balance sheet date), measured in accordance with accounting standards. It represents the total volume of assets existing in financial form for the enterprise and is a significant asset item on the balance sheet.

nodes.name: Total Financial Assets at Beginning of Period
nodes.definition: Total financial assets at the beginning of the period refers to the aggregate carrying amount of all financial assets held by an enterprise at the start of a specific accounting period (such as a fiscal year or quarter). It is typically derived directly from the carrying amount of financial assets at the end of the previous accounting period and serves as a fundamental data point on the balance sheet.

nodes.name: Total Financial Assets at Period Start
Total Financial Liabilities
nodes.definition: Total financial liabilities refer to the aggregate book value of all financial liabilities that an entity is obligated to settle by delivering cash or other financial assets at a specific point in time (e.g., the balance sheet date). It typically includes short-term borrowings, long-term borrowings, bonds payable, etc., and serves as a fundamental financial metric reflecting the scale of an enterprise's financing-related debt.

nodes.name: Total Financing
nodes.definition: Total financing refers to the aggregate sum of funds raised by an enterprise through various channels, including long-term and short-term, equity and debt financing. It serves as the basis for calculating metrics such as cost of capital and financing expense ratios, reflecting the total scale of external capital obtained by the enterprise within a specific period.

formulas.source_formula: Total Financing = Long-term Equity Investment + Long-term Debt Investment + Short-term Equity Investment + Short-term Debt Investment

nodes.name: Total Financing Cash Flow
nodes.definition: Total financing cash flow refers to the sum of cash flows generated by a company through debt and equity financing over a specific period.

formulas.source_formula: Total Financing Cash Flow = Net Debt Financing Cash Flow + Net Equity Financing Cash Flow

nodes.name: Total Fixed Asset Investment of Whole People-Owned Units
aliases: Fixed Asset Investment of the Whole People Ownership Units
Total Fixed Asset Investment of State-owned Units
全民所有制固定资产投资总额
国有单位固定资产投资总额
国有经济固定资产投资总额
nodes.definition: Total Fixed Asset Investment of Whole People-Owned Units refers to the sum, expressed in monetary terms, of the workload and related expenses for constructing and acquiring fixed assets completed by whole people-owned units (i.e., state-owned units) within a specific period (usually one year). It is a core indicator for measuring the scale, structure, and pace of investment in the state-owned economic sector.

nodes.name: Total Fixed Cost
nodes.definition: Total fixed cost refers to the aggregate cost that remains constant within a certain production range and does not vary with changes in output. It represents the fixed expenses a company must bear to maintain operations, typically calculated by summing all fixed cost items or by deducting the variable cost portion from total cost.

nodes.name: Total Fixed Costs
nodes.definition: Total fixed costs refer to costs whose total amount remains unchanged regardless of increases or decreases in business volume within a certain period and a certain range of activity levels. It is a core concept in cost behavior analysis, used to distinguish the fixed and variable components within total costs.

formulas.source_formula: Total Fixed Costs = Low-Point Activity Cost - Unit Variable Cost × Low-Point Activity Level

nodes.name: Total Fixed Costs of New Plan
aliases: Total Fixed Cost of New Plan
nodes.definition: Total fixed costs of the new plan refer to the aggregate costs that are expected to remain unchanged within a specific period and a defined range of business activity volume when a company implements a new operational plan or investment project, regardless of fluctuations in business volume. It represents the additional or adjusted portion of fixed costs attributable to adopting the new plan, relative to the original plan or baseline scenario.

nodes.name: Total Fixed Costs of Original Plan
nodes.definition: Total Fixed Costs of Original Plan refers to the sum of those costs that remain unchanged within a specific period and a certain range of business volume under a particular business plan or scheme (i.e., the 'Original Plan'), unaffected by increases or decreases in business volume. It serves as a benchmark value when evaluating changes to the plan, such as an increase in fixed costs.

nodes.name: Total Fixed Ordering Cost
nodes.definition: Total fixed ordering cost refers to the sum of fixed expenses that a company must incur to complete a single ordering activity, which are independent of the order quantity. These costs typically include order processing fees, purchasing staff salaries, information system usage fees, etc., and do not vary with changes in the quantity ordered each time.

nodes.name: Total Fixed Transportation Costs
nodes.definition: Total fixed transportation costs refer to the sum of transportation costs whose total amount does not vary with changes in transportation volume (such as ton-kilometers or freight mileage) within a certain period and a defined range of business activity. These costs typically include depreciation of transportation equipment, fixed lease payments, fixed personnel salaries, insurance premiums, etc., and constitute a fundamental data item in cost behavior analysis.

nodes.name: Total Foreign Demand in Current Period
nodes.definition: Total foreign demand in the current period refers to the aggregate demand for final goods and services produced by the domestic country (or economy) from the rest of the world and other countries/regions during a specific statistical period (such as a quarter or a year). It is a key macroeconomic indicator measuring the pulling effect of external markets on the domestic economy.

nodes.name: Total Frequency
nodes.definition: Total frequency refers to the sum of frequencies across all groups or categories in statistical analysis, which equals the total number of units or observations included in the study population.

nodes.name: Total Fund Profit
nodes.definition: Total Fund Profit is a composite metric that refers to the aggregate final financial results achieved by a fund through investment operations and other activities over a specific accounting period or its entire lifespan. It is typically not a single, directly obtained data point but is calculated using specific financial formulas, such as subtracting total expenses or costs from the fund's total revenue. In alternative investment funds like private equity, this metric serves as the critical basis for calculating the General Partner's performance fee (carried interest).

formulas.source_formula: Total Fund Profit = Operating Profit + Non-operating Income - Non-operating Expenses

nodes.name: Total Fund Value
nodes.definition: Total Fund Value refers to the aggregate market value of all assets held by a fund at a specific point in time (typically the valuation date), including its holdings of stocks, bonds, bank deposits, and other marketable securities, and serves as the basis for calculating the fund's net asset value.

nodes.name: Total Funds
nodes.definition: Total funds refer to the aggregate sum of all capital raised by an enterprise through various channels and methods, which can be utilized for production, operation, and investment activities. It reflects the overall scale of financial resources at the enterprise's disposal.

formulas.source_formula: Total Gas Fee = Units of Gas × (Base Fee + Priority Fee)
Total Growth = Principal × (1 + Interest Rate) ^ Years

nodes.name: Total Headcount
nodes.definition: Total headcount refers to the aggregate number of all individuals within a specific scope, group, or organization. In the accounting and finance field, it is commonly used to calculate per capita metrics, analyze human resource costs, or estimate market capacity.

formulas.source_formula: Total Hedge Fund Fee = AUM Fee + Performance Fee

nodes.name: Total Holding Period Return
nodes.definition: Total Holding Period Return refers to the absolute sum of all returns earned by an investment asset over a specific holding period. It typically includes dividend income, interest income, capital gains, and other cash or non-cash returns. It is a composite metric calculated via formulas, used for comprehensive investment performance evaluation. This concept is frequently cited in the calculation of total stock return.

operands.metric: Total Cash Return During Holding Period

formulas.source_formula: Total Holding Period Return = Total Cash Return During Holding Period + (Ending Investment Value - Beginning Investment Value)

nodes.name: Total Household Income
nodes.definition: Total household income refers to the sum of wage income, business income, property income, and transfer income obtained by all cohabiting family members in a surveyed household during a specific reporting period. It is a fundamental composite indicator for calculating household disposable income.

formulas.source_formula: Total Household Income = Wage Income + Business Income + Property Income + Transfer Income

nodes.name: Total Imports of Goods and Services
nodes.definition: Total imports of goods and services refers to the total value of all goods and services purchased from foreign countries by a country or region within a specific period (usually a year or a quarter). It reflects the scale of the country's demand for foreign goods and services and is a key component of the current account in the balance of payments.

nodes.name: Total Indirect Costs
nodes.definition: Total indirect costs refer to the aggregate of all expenses incurred by an enterprise over a specific period for organizing and managing production and operational activities. These costs cannot be directly attributed to specific products or services and must be allocated according to certain criteria. They typically do not directly participate in the production of specific goods but are essential for overall operations.

nodes.name: Total Indirect Costs to be Allocated
nodes.definition: Total indirect costs to be allocated refers to the sum of all indirect costs incurred by an enterprise during a specific costing period that have not yet been assigned to specific cost objects (such as products, services, or departments) according to a certain standard. These costs cannot be directly attributed to a specific object and must be apportioned using an allocation rate.

nodes.name: Total Initial Investment
nodes.definition: Total initial investment refers to the total amount of capital invested by an enterprise or individual at the commencement of a project. It typically includes components such as fixed asset investment and working capital investment, and is used to reflect the total input cost during the project initiation phase. It is a key metric in capital budgeting and investment decision-making.

formulas.source_formula: Total Initial Investment = Construction Investment + Working Capital Investment
Total Initial Investment = Number of Shares × Initial Share Price
Total Initial Investment = Cost of Forming Fixed Assets + Cost of Forming Intangible Assets + Cost of Forming Other Assets + Contingency Reserve + Working Capital Investment

nodes.name: Total Interest
nodes.definition: Total interest refers to the aggregate amount of all interest payments a borrower is required to make over the entire loan period. It is commonly found in financial products such as loans and bonds, with the specific amount determined by factors including principal amount, interest rate level, interest accrual period, and repayment method (e.g., equal principal and interest payments or equal principal payments).

formulas.source_formula: Total Interest = Principal × Annual Interest Rate × Time
Total Interest = Initial Interest + Future Interest
Total Interest = Total Payment - Purchase Price
Total Interest = Principal × Annual Interest Rate × Loan Term (years)
Total Interest = Face Value × Coupon Rate × Years
Total Interest = Loan Principal × Annual Interest Rate × (Loan Term (Months) ÷ 12)

nodes.name: Total Interest (Hire Purchase)
nodes.definition: Total interest in a hire purchase agreement is the cumulative finance charge paid by the buyer, measured as the excess of total payments (including down payment and installments) over the cash purchase price of the asset. It reflects the cost of financing under hire purchase and typically excludes separate fees or penalties unless they are included in the total payments.

nodes.name: Total Interest Expense
nodes.definition: Total interest expense refers to the aggregate sum of all interest costs that an accounting entity (such as a company or individual) is required to pay to creditors over a specific period due to borrowed funds (e.g., loans, bonds).

nodes.name: Total Interest Income
nodes.definition: Total interest income refers to the aggregate amount of interest compensation earned over a specific period for providing the right to use funds (e.g., through loans or investments), typically calculated based on principal, interest rate, and time.

formulas.source_formula: Total Interest Income = Principal × Annual Interest Rate × Time

nodes.name: Total Interest Paid
nodes.definition: Total interest paid is the aggregate amount of interest a borrower pays over the full mortgage term. It equals the total of all monthly payments made over the loan term minus the original principal amount.

formulas.source_formula: Total Interest Paid = (Monthly Payment × Total Payments) - Principal
Total Interest Paid = Monthly Interest Rate × Cumulative Outstanding Principal
Total Interest Paid = (Monthly Payment × Term Months) - Principal
Total Interest Paid = Interest Payment per Period × Term Years × Payment Frequency
Total Interest Paid = Payment × Months - (Beginning Balance - Ending Balance)
Total Interest to Date = Total Interest to Date (Prior) + Interest Payment

nodes.name: Total Interest-Bearing Debt
nodes.definition: Total interest-bearing debt refers to the sum of all principal amounts of debt for which a company is obligated to pay interest, primarily including bank borrowings, issued bonds, and other liability items requiring regular interest payments. It is a fundamental figure on the balance sheet that directly reflects the true scale of debt on which the company incurs interest costs.

nodes.name: Total Interest-Bearing Debt of Previous Period
nodes.definition: Total interest-bearing debt of the previous period refers to the aggregate book value of all debt obligations requiring interest payments at the end of the preceding accounting period (such as the previous year, quarter, or month). These obligations typically include bank borrowings, issued bonds, finance lease liabilities under long-term payables, etc.

nodes.name: Total Interest-Bearing Liabilities
nodes.definition: Total interest-bearing liabilities refer to the sum of all debts on which a company must pay interest, typically including short-term borrowings, long-term liabilities due within one year, long-term borrowings, bonds payable, and long-term payables. These liabilities constitute a significant component of a company's financing costs.

nodes.name: Total Interest-Bearing Liabilities at Beginning of Next Period
aliases: Opening Interest-bearing Debt of Next Period
Total Interest-bearing Liabilities at Beginning of Next Period
下期期初付息负债合计
nodes.definition: Total interest-bearing liabilities at the beginning of the next period refers to the aggregate book value of all debt obligations requiring interest payments at the start of the next accounting period (e.g., next month, next quarter, or next year). These obligations typically include short-term borrowings, current portion of long-term debt, long-term borrowings, bonds payable, and long-term payables.

nodes.name: Total Interest-Free Liabilities at Period End
nodes.definition: Total interest-free liabilities at period end refers to the aggregate amount of all liability items that do not require interest payments at the conclusion of a specific accounting period (such as quarter-end or year-end). These liabilities typically include operating liabilities such as accounts payable, advance receipts, contract liabilities, employee compensation payable, and taxes payable.

nodes.name: Total Interest-bearing Debt for the Period
aliases: Total Interest-Bearing Debt for the Current Period
nodes.definition: Total interest-bearing debt for the period refers to the aggregate amount of all debt obligations on which interest must be paid during the current accounting period (such as the current quarter or fiscal year). These obligations typically include bank borrowings, issued bonds, and financing lease liabilities under long-term payables.

nodes.name: Total Interest-bearing Debt in Current Period
Total Interest-bearing Debt in Prior Period
Total Interest-bearing Liabilities at Next Period-end
aliases: Total Interest-Bearing Liabilities at Next Period End
未来期间有息负债总额
nodes.definition: Total interest-bearing liabilities at next period-end refers to the aggregate book value of all debt obligations requiring interest payments at the conclusion of the next accounting period (such as the next fiscal year, quarter, or month). These obligations typically include short-term borrowings, long-term liabilities due within one year, long-term borrowings, bonds payable, and long-term payables.

nodes.name: Total Interest-bearing Liabilities at the Beginning of the Next Period
Total Interest-bearing Liabilities at the End of the Next Period

formulas.source_formula: Total Intrinsic Value = Intrinsic Value per Share × 100 × Number of Contracts

nodes.name: Total Inventory Cost
nodes.definition: Total inventory cost refers to all costs incurred by an enterprise in inventory management, including acquisition cost, holding cost, and shortage cost.

formulas.source_formula: Total Inventory Cost = Acquisition Cost + Holding Cost + Shortage Cost

Total Inventory Cost = Fixed Ordering Cost + (Annual Demand × Variable Ordering Cost per Order) ÷ Order Quantity + Annual Demand × Unit Price + Fixed Holding Cost + (Order Quantity ÷ 2) × Variable Holding Cost per Unit + Shortage Cost

nodes.name: Total Invested Capital
nodes.definition: Total invested capital refers to the book value of all funds invested in the business by all investors (including creditors and shareholders), representing the total capital employed by the enterprise to generate profits. It excludes non-interest-bearing liabilities such as accounts payable arising from trade credit. Its concept is essentially consistent with 'Capital Employed'.

formulas.source_formula: Total Invested Capital = Shareholders' Equity + Total Interest-bearing Debt
Total Invested Capital = Fixed Assets + Working Capital
Total Invested Capital = Working Capital + Net Long-term Assets - Non-interest-bearing Long-term Liabilities

nodes.name: Total Investment
nodes.definition: Total investment refers to the total value of an investment at a specific future point in time, reflecting the cumulative result of the initial investment amount after considering the compound interest effect. In project investment evaluation, it also refers to the sum of the original total investment and capitalized interest during the construction period, serving as a value indicator to measure the overall scale of project investment.

formulas.source_formula: Total Investment = Investment Amount × (1 + Investment Return Rate) ^ Investment Period

nodes.name: Total Investment Amount
nodes.definition: Total investment amount refers to the entire capital invested to achieve a specific investment objective. It is a composite metric that can be calculated using different underlying data. Its specific composition and calculation method vary depending on the investment target (e.g., project, security) and the purpose of the calculation (e.g., initial investment, terminal value).

formulas.source_formula: Total Investment Amount = (Annual Product Output × Product Unit Price) ÷ Capital Turnover Rate

nodes.name: Total Investment Amount Agreed by Limited Partners
Total Investment Assets
nodes.definition: Total Investment Assets is a composite financial metric, typically calculated by summing the market values of various investment assets (such as cash, stocks, bonds, real estate, etc.). It is used to measure the total scale of investment assets in a portfolio or enterprise. It is a non-leaf node indicator and is referenced in alternative investment analysis.

formulas.source_formula: Total Investment Assets = Cash and Cash Equivalents + Stock Investments + Bond Investments + Real Estate Investments + Other Alternative Investment Assets

nodes.name: Total Investment Cost
nodes.definition: Total investment cost refers to the entire capital expenditure incurred to complete an investment activity, including the initial principal investment and related direct expenses such as transaction fees and taxes. When considering the time value of money, it can also refer to the total future value of the investment principal compounded at the expected rate of return until the end of the investment period.

formulas.source_formula: Total Investment Cost = Construction Investment + Working Capital Investment
Total Investment Cost = Investment Amount × (1 + Investment Return Rate) ^ Investment Period

nodes.name: Total Investment Expenditure
nodes.definition: Total investment expenditure refers to the aggregate sum of cash or cash equivalents paid by an enterprise or individual to acquire, construct, or upgrade long-term assets (such as plants, equipment, technology, etc.) and to undertake other investment projects (such as purchasing stocks, funds). It typically includes all directly related outlays such as purchase costs, associated transaction fees, taxes, and reflects the total initial capital invested to initiate or sustain an investment activity.

nodes.name: Total Investment Income
nodes.definition: Total investment income refers to the aggregate amount of all returns earned by an enterprise through external investment activities (such as holding or selling financial assets like stocks, bonds, and funds, as well as equity investments) within a specific accounting period. It typically includes dividends, interest income, realized gains or losses from the disposal of investment assets, and is a key item on the income statement reflecting the results of the enterprise's investment activities.

nodes.name: Total Investment Requirement for the Current Period
nodes.definition: Total investment requirement for the current period refers to the total amount of net operating assets that a company needs to invest additionally to support the expected growth in operating activities. It is typically calculated as the difference between the projected net operating assets and the base period net operating assets, or as the product of the base period net operating assets and the operating revenue growth rate. It is a core indicator in financial forecasting and financing planning.

formulas.source_formula: Total Investment Requirement for the Current Period = Base Period Net Operating Assets × Operating Revenue Growth Rate
Total Investment Requirement for the Current Period = Projected Net Operating Assets - Base Period Net Operating Assets
Total Investment Requirement for the Current Period = (Projected Operating Assets - Projected Operating Liabilities) - (Base Period Operating Assets - Base Period Operating Liabilities)

nodes.name: Total Issue Amount
nodes.definition: Total Issue Amount refers to the total funds raised by a company from investors through the issuance of securities such as stocks or bonds. It is determined at the time of issuance, typically derived directly from the issuance contract or announcement, and serves as the basis for calculating issuance expenses and net proceeds.

nodes.name: Total Issued Common Shares
nodes.definition: Total issued common shares refers to the total number of common stock shares that a company has issued to investors and are outstanding in the market. It is fundamental data in a company's capital structure, typically disclosed directly in financial statements or equity information, and serves as a crucial original basis for calculating financial metrics such as earnings per share and market capitalization.

nodes.name: Total Issued Shares
nodes.definition: Total issued shares refers to the aggregate number of all types of shares that a company has issued and outstanding. It represents the foundation of the company's capital structure and is a figure directly derived from the company's issuance records, not calculated through formulas.

nodes.name: Total Labor Input
nodes.definition: Total labor input refers to the quantified sum of all labor resources invested by an enterprise or organization to complete production and operational activities within a specific period. It is typically expressed as total labor time (e.g., total man-hours) or total labor cost, serving as fundamental raw data for measuring the scale of labor input, which can be directly obtained from business records such as attendance logs and payrolls.

nodes.name: Total Lead Time
nodes.definition: Total lead time refers to the entire duration from when a customer places an order until the complete delivery of the product or service to the customer. It encompasses the time consumed in all stages including order processing, manufacturing, and logistics transportation.

nodes.name: Total Liabilities
nodes.definition: Total liabilities represent the sum of all liabilities, including current liabilities, long-term liabilities, etc. It is a key indicator on the balance sheet, reflecting the total debt obligations of an enterprise or individual, and is a composite metric rather than a fundamental raw data point.

formulas.source_formula: Total Liabilities = Current Liabilities + Non-current Liabilities
Total Liabilities = Current Liabilities + Long-term Liabilities

nodes.name: Total Liabilities at Beginning of Next Period
nodes.definition: Total liabilities at the beginning of the next period refer to the aggregate amount of all present obligations of an enterprise at the start of the next accounting period (such as the next month, quarter, or year), which are expected to result in an outflow of economic benefits in the future.

nodes.name: Total Liabilities at Beginning of Period
nodes.definition: Total liabilities at the beginning of a period refer to the aggregate value of present obligations that an entity is expected to result in an outflow of economic benefits, as recorded at the start of a specific accounting period (such as a fiscal year or quarter). This figure is directly taken from the total liabilities at the end of the previous period as reported in financial statements (e.g., the balance sheet) and serves as the baseline data for financial analysis in the current period.

nodes.name: Total Liabilities at Beginning of Year
aliases: Total Liabilities at the Beginning of the Year
nodes.definition: Total liabilities at the beginning of the year refers to the aggregate book value of all debts and obligations assumed by an enterprise at the start of a fiscal year (typically January 1st). It is directly sourced from the balance sheet and serves as fundamental data reflecting the initial state of the enterprise's financial structure.

nodes.name: Total Liabilities at End of First Quarter
aliases: Total Liabilities at the End of Q1
nodes.definition: Total liabilities at the end of the first quarter refer to the aggregate value of present obligations arising from past transactions or events, which are expected to result in an outflow of economic benefits from the enterprise, as reported at the financial reporting date of the first quarter (typically January 1 to March 31). It reflects all debts assumed by the enterprise at the end of the first quarter and is generally calculated by directly summing the ending balances of all liability accounts from the accounting ledgers.

nodes.name: Total Liabilities at End of Q2
Total Liabilities at End of Second Quarter
aliases: Total Liabilities at the End of Q2
nodes.definition: Total liabilities at the end of the second quarter refer to the aggregate book value of all liabilities recognized and consolidated according to accounting books and standards at the conclusion of the second fiscal quarter (typically June 30). This figure reflects the total present obligations of the enterprise at a specific point in time that are expected to result in an outflow of economic benefits, and is generally directly reported under the 'Total Liabilities' line item on the balance sheet.

nodes.name: Total Liabilities at Next Period End
aliases: Total Liabilities at the End of Next Period
未来期间期末负债总额
nodes.definition: Total Liabilities at Next Period End refers to the aggregate sum of present obligations arising from past transactions or events, which are expected to result in an outflow of economic benefits from the enterprise, as of the end of the next accounting period (such as the next quarter, half-year, or fiscal year). It includes both current liabilities and non-current liabilities (or long-term liabilities).

nodes.name: Total Liabilities at Period End
nodes.definition: Total liabilities at period end refer to the present obligations of an enterprise arising from past transactions or events, the settlement of which is expected to result in an outflow of economic benefits from the enterprise, including current liabilities and non-current liabilities. It is a key item on the balance sheet, reflecting the debt level and financial risk of the enterprise.

formulas.source_formula: Total Liabilities at Period End = Current Liabilities + Non-current Liabilities

nodes.name: Total Liabilities at Year-end
nodes.definition: Total liabilities at year-end refer to the aggregate present obligations of an enterprise at the end of an accounting year, arising from past transactions or events, which are expected to result in an outflow of economic benefits. This includes both current liabilities and non-current liabilities. It is a key component of the balance sheet, reflecting the company's financial leverage and debt repayment risk.

formulas.source_formula: Total Liabilities at Year-end = Current Liabilities + Non-current Liabilities

nodes.name: Total Liabilities at the Beginning of the Next Period
Total Liabilities at the End of the First Quarter
Total Liabilities at the End of the Next Period
Total Liabilities for the Current Period
nodes.definition: Total liabilities for the current period refer to the present obligations of an enterprise arising from past transactions or events, the settlement of which is expected to result in an outflow of economic benefits from the enterprise, including current liabilities and non-current liabilities, as of a specific accounting period (e.g., the end of the current period). It is a core item on the balance sheet, reflecting the debt level and financial risk of the enterprise.

formulas.source_formula: Total Liabilities for the Current Period = Current Liabilities + Non-current Liabilities
Total Liabilities for the Current Period = Total Assets - Total Equity

nodes.name: Total Liabilities of Previous Period
nodes.definition: Total Liabilities of Previous Period refers to the aggregate amount of liability items directly recorded in the balance sheet at the end of the prior accounting period (such as the previous fiscal year, quarter, or month), reflecting the total debt obligations the company was required to repay in the future as of the end of the prior period.

nodes.name: Total Liabilities of Subsidiary
nodes.definition: Total Liabilities of Subsidiary is an aggregate measure of all liability items of a subsidiary at the balance sheet date, calculated by summing current liabilities and non-current liabilities. It reflects the subsidiary's debt burden and financial risk, and is commonly used in consolidated financial statements and financial structure analysis.

nodes.name: Total Loan Amount
nodes.definition: Total loan amount refers to the aggregate principal amount of all loans obtained by a borrower from financial institutions (such as banks), or the sum of outstanding loan principal at a specific point in time. It represents the portion of the borrower's total liabilities attributable to loans and serves as the basis for interest calculation and repayment schedule formulation.

formulas.source_formula: Total Loan Amount = Principal + Total Interest

nodes.name: Total Loan Term
nodes.definition: Total loan term refers to the total number of years planned or actually taken for a borrower to repay the loan principal and interest in full, from the commencement of repayment to the final settlement. It is a core parameter in loan agreements, directly impacting the periodic repayment amount and total interest expense.

nodes.name: Total Loan with Up-Front Mortgage Insurance (UFMI)
aliases: Total Loan Including Upfront Mortgage Insurance
一次性按揭保险费并入后的贷款总额
包含前期抵押贷款保险费的贷款总额
nodes.definition: Total Loan with Up-Front Mortgage Insurance (UFMI) represents the mortgage principal after the up-front mortgage insurance premium is financed into the balance. It equals the original loan amount plus the UFMI premium, and it impacts interest accrual and monthly payments, commonly in FHA-backed mortgages where the upfront premium may be rolled into the loan.

formulas.source_formula: Total Loan with Up-Front Mortgage Insurance (UFMI) = Loan Amount + Up-Front Mortgage Insurance Premium

nodes.name: Total Long-term Assets
nodes.definition: Total Long-term Assets refers to the aggregate value of all assets held by an enterprise that are expected to be realized, sold, or consumed over a period longer than one operating cycle (typically exceeding one year). It reflects the scale of resources allocated by the enterprise for long-term operations and investments.

nodes.name: Total Long-term Operating Liabilities of Previous Period
nodes.definition: Total Long-term Operating Liabilities of Previous Period refers to the aggregate amount of all liabilities with a repayment term exceeding one year that were incurred to support the enterprise's daily business operations, as of the end of the previous accounting period (such as the prior fiscal year or quarter). These liabilities are typically related to the core business operations of the enterprise, such as long-term accounts payable and long-term advances received, and exclude long-term liabilities arising from investment or financing activities.

nodes.name: Total Management Fee
nodes.definition: Total management fee refers to the aggregate of all expenses incurred by an enterprise for organizing and managing production and operational activities. It is typically calculated based on a calculation base and a management fee rate, and serves as a key component in evaluating corporate operating costs and portfolio costs.

formulas.source_formula: Total Management Fee = Calculation Base × Management Fee Rate

nodes.name: Total Manufacturing Cost at Low Point
nodes.definition: Total manufacturing cost at low point refers to the total manufacturing cost corresponding to the lowest level of activity (such as production volume or machine hours) during a selected period in cost behavior analysis (e.g., the high-low method). It serves as one of the fundamental data points for decomposing mixed costs and calculating unit variable costs and fixed costs.

nodes.name: Total Manufacturing Overhead
nodes.definition: Total manufacturing overhead refers to the sum of all direct material costs, direct labor costs, and indirect manufacturing costs incurred during the production process. It is a core component of production cost accounting, used for accurately accumulating and allocating production expenses.

nodes.name: Total Manufacturing Overhead at High Point
Total Manufacturing Overhead at Low Point
Total Market Capitalization
nodes.definition: Total market capitalization refers to the total value of all outstanding shares of a listed company calculated at market prices, reflecting the company's size, market position, and investment value. It is a core composite indicator in financial and investment analysis.

nodes.name: Total Market Capitalization at Reporting Date
nodes.definition: Total market capitalization at the reporting date refers to the total market value of all outstanding shares of a listed company calculated at the prevailing market price during a specific reporting period. It is used to reflect the company's scale and industry position, and serves as a key indicator for calculating the base period index.

nodes.name: Total Market Capitalization of Equity Securities
nodes.definition: Total market capitalization of equity securities refers to the aggregate market value of all equity securities, calculated by summing the product of the market price of each equity security and its number of shares outstanding. It is a key composite metric for measuring capital market size, company value, and portfolio risk, widely used in valuation, risk management, and asset allocation.

nodes.name: Total Market Portfolio Value
nodes.definition: Total market portfolio value refers to the aggregate value of all investable assets (typically all issued stocks) in a specific market, calculated at their market prices. It represents the overall scale of the market and serves as the basis for calculating metrics such as market weights and market portfolio returns.

nodes.name: Total Market Sales
nodes.definition: Total market sales refers to the aggregate revenue amount generated by all participants (such as companies, product lines, or industries) within a specific market through the sale of goods or provision of services over a defined period.

nodes.name: Total Market Value
nodes.definition: Total Market Value is the sum of the market value of equity capital and debt capital, reflecting the overall valuation of a company in the market. It is commonly used in cost of capital calculations, enterprise value assessment, and financial management analysis.

nodes.name: Total Market Value of Equity
nodes.definition: Total market value of equity refers to the aggregate market value of all outstanding shares of a company at a specific point in time, typically calculated by multiplying the total number of shares outstanding by the current market price per share. It reflects the market's assessment of the company's overall value.

nodes.name: Total Market Value of Equity Securities
Total Market Value of Long-term Bonds
nodes.definition: Total market value of long-term bonds refers to the current aggregate market value of all bonds issued by a company with remaining maturities exceeding one year. It reflects the market's overall valuation of these long-term debt instruments and serves as a key metric for assessing a company's long-term debt scale and capital structure.

nodes.name: Total Market Value of Long-term Debt Securities
nodes.definition: Total market value of long-term debt securities refers to the aggregate value of all outstanding long-term debt securities (such as bonds, long-term notes, etc.) issued by a company, calculated at current market prices. It reflects the overall valuation of debt securities by investors in the capital market and is used to measure the scale of corporate debt financing and market risk exposure.

nodes.name: Total Market Value of Short-term Debt
nodes.definition: Total Market Value of Short-term Debt refers to the aggregate market value of all short-term debt obligations (i.e., current liabilities such as short-term borrowings, notes payable, long-term debt due within one year, etc.) of a company in the financial markets. It reflects the market's valuation of these short-term obligations, rather than their book value as reported on financial statements.

nodes.name: Total Market Value of the Company
aliases: Total Market Value of the Firm
nodes.definition: Total market value of the company refers to the overall valuation of the company in the public market, reflecting the market's comprehensive expectation of the company's future wealth creation capacity. In capital structure analysis, it is typically defined as the sum of the market value of equity capital and the market value of debt capital, serving as a key indicator for determining the optimal capital structure in the corporate value analysis method.

operands.metric: Total Face Value of Debt Issued
Percentage of Market Value to Face Value of Debt

formulas.source_formula: Total Market Value of the Company = Number of Common Shares Outstanding × Market Price per Common Share + Total Face Value of Debt Issued × Percentage of Market Value to Face Value of Debt

nodes.name: Total Market Value of the Portfolio
Total Material Consumption in the Past Three Years
Total Material Consumption in the Previous Three Years
aliases: Total Material Consumption of the Past Three Years
过去三年材料总消耗量
nodes.definition: Total material consumption in the previous three years refers to the aggregate quantity or monetary value of various raw materials and auxiliary materials actually consumed by an enterprise for production, operations, and other activities during the past three complete fiscal years. It is a fundamental statistic derived from historical business records, used for analyzing consumption trends and establishing quota standards.

formulas.source_formula: Total Mill Levy = (School District Revenue + County Revenue + City Revenue) ÷ Total Assessed Property Value

nodes.name: Total Monthly Aggregate Deductible
aliases: 总额停损保险月度总免赔额
nodes.definition: Total monthly aggregate deductible is the employer’s cumulative deductible for a given month under an aggregate stop-loss insurance arrangement. It is computed by multiplying the monthly deductible per employee by the number of enrolled employees, and represents the threshold of employer liability before aggregate stop-loss coverage attaches for that month.

formulas.source_formula: Total Monthly Aggregate Deductible = Monthly Deductible per Employee × Number of Enrolled Employees

nodes.name: Total Monthly Customer Repayment Amount
nodes.definition: Total Monthly Customer Repayment Amount refers to the aggregate sum of all loan or installment payments that a customer is required to repay within a specified period (typically one month). It reflects the customer's fixed monthly debt expenditure level and serves as a crucial indicator for assessing their repayment capacity and credit risk.

nodes.name: Total Mortgage Insurance Premium (MIP)
nodes.definition: Total Mortgage Insurance Premium (MIP) refers to the cumulative mortgage insurance charges paid over a specified period. It is computed as the mortgage loan principal multiplied by the annual mortgage insurance premium rate and the number of years. This metric captures the total cost of ongoing MIP typically applicable to FHA-insured loans and is distinct from Up-Front Mortgage Insurance (UFMI), which is a one-time premium paid at closing.

formulas.source_formula: Total Mortgage Insurance Premium = Loan Amount × Mortgage Insurance Premium Rate × Years
Total Movement = Open Price - Low Price

operands.metric: Social Security and Medicare Taxes (Employer + Employee)

formulas.source_formula: Total Nanny Tax = Social Security and Medicare Taxes (Employer + Employee) + FUTA Tax

nodes.name: Total Net Assets
nodes.definition: Total net assets refer to the residual portion of a company's total assets after deducting total liabilities, representing the economic interests that the owners (shareholders) hold in the company's assets.

nodes.name: Total Net Assets at Period End
nodes.definition: Total net assets at period end refers to the total equity attributable to owners (shareholders) that remains after subtracting total liabilities from total assets at the conclusion of a specific accounting period (such as month-end, quarter-end, or year-end). It represents the true value of wealth belonging to the owners at that point in time.

nodes.name: Total Net Cash Flow
nodes.definition: Total net cash flow refers to the net amount of total inflows minus total outflows of cash and cash equivalents within a specific period. It reflects the net increase or decrease in cash during that period and is a core indicator for measuring a company's cash flow position.

nodes.name: Total Net Cash Outflow under 30-Day Stress Scenario
aliases: Net cash outflow over 30 days under stress scenario
nodes.definition: This concept refers to the difference between the total expected cash outflows and the total expected cash inflows over the next 30 days under the stress scenario defined for the Liquidity Coverage Ratio. It is commonly used to calculate regulatory metrics such as the Liquidity Coverage Ratio and is a core composite indicator in liquidity risk management.

formulas.source_formula: Total Net Cash Outflow under 30-Day Stress Scenario = Total Expected Cash Outflows - Total Expected Cash Inflows
Total Net Cash Outflow under 30-Day Stress Scenario = Total Expected Cash Outflows - min(Total Expected Cash Inflows, 75% × Total Expected Cash Outflows)

nodes.name: Total Net Income Over Multiple Years
Total Net Operating Assets
nodes.definition: Total net operating assets refers to the net value of assets used in business operations minus corresponding liabilities, reflecting the enterprise's ability to create value through operating activities.

formulas.source_formula: Total Net Operating Assets = Net Debt + Owners' Equity
Total Net Operating Assets = Operating Assets - Operating Liabilities
supporting_source_formulas: Total Net Operating Assets = Operating Assets - Operating Liabilities

formulas.source_formula: Total Net Operating Assets = Operating Working Capital + Net Operating Long-term Assets
Total Net Operating Assets = (Operating Current Assets + Operating Current Liabilities) + (Operating Long-term Assets - Operating Long-term Liabilities)

nodes.name: Total Net Profit
